title.raw: 卷八十九 列傳第五十九 忠義 Volume 89 Biographies 59: Loyalty and Righteousness

sentences.zh: 序

translations.literal: Preface
translations.idiomatic: Preface

sentences.zh: 古人有言：「君子殺身以成仁，不求生以害仁。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "The gentleman sacrifices his own life to complete benevolence; he does not seek to preserve life at the expense of benevolence."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients put it this way: the gentleman gives his life to fulfill humaneness; he does not cling to survival if it would violate humaneness.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「非死之難，處死之難。

translations.literal: " It is also said: "It is not dying that is difficult; bearing death rightly is difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Another line runs: dying is not the hard part—meeting death as one should is the hard part.

sentences.zh: 」信哉斯言也！

translations.literal: " How true these words are!
translations.idiomatic: Those words hold true.

sentences.zh: 是知隕節苟合其宜，義夫豈吝其沒；

translations.literal: From this one knows: if casting aside one's integrity happens to fit what is right, would a man of duty begrudge his perishing?
translations.idiomatic: Thus we see that when holding fast to integrity suits the right course, a man of principle does not shrink from paying with his life.

sentences.zh: 捐軀若得其所，烈士不愛其存。

translations.literal: If giving up the body obtains its proper place, a resolute man does not cling to mere survival.
translations.idiomatic: When sacrifice meets its proper moment, a steadfast man does not treasure existence for its own sake.

sentences.zh: 故能守鐵石之深衷，厲松筠之雅操，見貞心於歲暮，標勁節于嚴風，赴鼎鑊其如歸，履危亡而不顧，書名竹帛，畫象丹青，前史以為美談，後來仰其徽烈者也。

translations.literal: Therefore they can keep an iron-and-stone loyalty within, cultivate the noble purity of pine and bamboo, show a steadfast heart in year's end, display unyielding integrity in harsh wind; they go to cauldron and hot iron as if returning home, tread peril and death without looking back; their names are written on bamboo and silk, their portraits painted in red and blue; earlier histories treat them as fine tales, and later ages look up to their shining merit.
translations.idiomatic: So they guard an unshakable resolve within, polish a virtue pure as pine and bamboo, prove constancy in the year's bitter end and unbending integrity in biting wind; they march to the cauldron as if going home and face ruin without flinching. Their names endure on bamboo slips and silk, their faces in scarlet and indigo portraiture—past chronicles cite them as exemplary tales, and posterity reveres their radiant deeds.

sentences.zh: 晉自元康之後，政亂朝昏，禍難薦興，艱虞孔熾，遂使奸凶放命，戎狄交侵，函夏沸騰，蒼生塗炭，干戈日用，戰爭方興。

translations.literal: From after the Yuankang era of Jin, government was chaotic and the court dark; disasters arose in succession and hardship blazed fiercely, so that villains threw off restraint and Rong and Di invaded in turn; the heartland seethed, the black-haired people were smeared with charcoal; arms were wielded daily and war had just begun to rise.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yuankang years, Jin fell into turmoil: the administration unraveled and the court grew dim; calamities piled up and distress burned hot. Villains defied authority, northern tribes took turns raiding the heartland, the realm convulsed, and common folk were ground to dust under ceaseless arms and spreading war.

sentences.zh: 雖背恩忘義之徒不可勝載，而蹈節輕生之士無乏于時。

translations.literal: Though men who betrayed grace and forgot duty could not be fully recorded, yet men who embraced integrity and held life lightly were not lacking in that age.
translations.idiomatic: Traitors who threw away obligation were beyond counting, yet men who chose principle over life were never absent in those same years.

sentences.zh: 至若嵇紹之衛難乘輿，卞壼之亡軀鋒鏑，桓雄之義高田叔，周崎之節邁解揚，羅丁致命於舊君，辛吉恥臣於戎虜，張禕引鴆以全節，王諒斷臂以厲忠，莫不志烈秋霜，精貫白日，足以激清風于萬古，厲薄俗于當年者歟！

translations.literal: As for Ji Shao shielding the imperial carriage in crisis, Bian Kun losing his body to spearheads and arrows, Huan Xiong, whose righteousness rivaled Tian Shu, Zhou Qi, whose integrity surpassed Jie Yang, Luo Ding laying down his life for his former lord, Xin Ji ashamed to serve barbarians as minister, Zhang Yi draining poison to preserve his integrity, Wang Liang severing an arm to steel his loyalty—all alike bore wills fierce as autumn frost and spirits piercing as the noon sun, enough to stir pure wind through ten thousand ages and shame shallow ways in their own day!
translations.idiomatic: Think of Ji Shao guarding the emperor's carriage in peril, Bian Kun falling to blades and shafts, Huan Xiong matching Tian Shu in devotion, Zhou Qi outdoing Jie Yang in steadfastness, Luo Ding dying for a former sovereign, Xin Ji refusing to bow to alien rulers, Zhang Yi drinking poison to keep his honor, Wang Liang cutting off an arm to prove his loyalty—each will like autumn frost, each spirit bright as noon, enough to quicken moral clarity for ages and shame a degenerate age.

sentences.zh: 所謂亂世識忠臣，斯之謂也。

translations.literal: What is called "in troubled times one recognizes loyal ministers" refers to this.
translations.idiomatic: This is what men mean when they say troubled times reveal who the loyal ministers are.

sentences.zh: 卞壼、劉超、鐘雅、周虓等已入列傳，其餘即敘其行事以為《忠義傳》，用旌晉氏之有人焉。

translations.literal: Bian Kun, Liu Chao, Zhong Ya, Zhou Xiao, and others have already entered the standard biographies; the rest are here narrated in conduct gathered as the "Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness," to signal that the House of Jin still had such men.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Kun, Liu Chao, Zhong Ya, Zhou Xiao, and the like already have full biographies elsewhere; those who remain are collected here under Loyalty and Righteousness to show that the Jin court could still claim men of honor.

sentences.zh: 嵇紹

translations.literal: Ji Shao
translations.idiomatic: Ji Shao

sentences.zh: 嵇紹，字延祖，魏中散大夫康之子也。

translations.literal: Ji Shao, courtesy name Yanzu, was the son of Wei Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary Ji Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Shao, whose courtesy name was Yanzu, was the son of Ji Kang, who had served Wei as Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 十歲而孤，事母孝謹。

translations.literal: At ten he was orphaned; he served his mother with filial care and reverence.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at age ten and thereafter honored his mother with scrupulous filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 以父得罪，靖居私門。

translations.literal: Because his father had offended, he lived quietly in private retirement.
translations.idiomatic: His father's disgrace kept him living quietly at home, outside office.

sentences.zh: 山濤領選，啟武帝曰：「《康誥》有言：'父子罪不相及。

translations.literal: Shan Tao headed personnel selection and reported to Emperor Wu: "The 'Announcements to Kang' says: 'Father and son do not visit guilt upon each other.'"
translations.idiomatic: When Shan Tao supervised appointments, he told Emperor Wu: the "Announcements to Kang" says fathers and sons do not answer for one another's crimes.

sentences.zh: '嵇紹賢侔郤缺，宜加旌命，請為秘書郎。

translations.literal: 'Ji Shao's worth equals that of Xi Que; he should receive a summons of commendation—request him as Palace Secretary.'"
translations.idiomatic: Ji Shao is as worthy as Xi Que; he deserves an imperial summons—please name him Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 」帝謂濤曰：「如卿所言，乃堪為丞，何但郎也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said to Shan Tao: "As you describe him, he could even serve as vice director—how could a mere secretary suffice?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied to Shan Tao: "If he is everything you say, he is fit to be vice director—why limit him to secretary?"

sentences.zh: 」乃發詔征之，起家為秘書丞。

translations.literal: " An edict was then issued summoning him; from common status he rose to Vice Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned him, and he entered service first as Vice Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 紹始入洛，或謂王戎曰：「昨于稠人中始見嵇紹，昂昂然如野鶴之在雞群。

translations.literal: When Shao first entered Luoyang, someone said to Wang Rong: "Yesterday amid the crowd I first saw Ji Shao—towering, like a wild crane among chickens."
translations.idiomatic: When Shao first arrived in Luoyang, someone remarked to Wang Rong: "Yesterday, in the press of people, I saw Ji Shao for the first time—stately as a crane among barnyard fowl."

sentences.zh: 」戎曰：「君復未見其父耳。

translations.literal: " Rong said: "You have still not seen his father."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong answered: "Then you have not met his father."

sentences.zh: 」累遷汝陰太守。

translations.literal: " He was promoted in stages to Administrator of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Administrator of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射裴頠亦深器之，每曰：「使延祖為吏部尚書，可使天下無復遺才矣。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Left of the Secretariat Pei Yi also deeply esteemed him, often saying: "Were Yanzu made Minister of Personnel, he could make it so the realm had no overlooked talent again."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yi, Vice Director of the Left of the Secretariat, thought the world of him and used to say: "Put Yanzu in charge of personnel and no able man in the empire would go unused."

sentences.zh: 」沛國戴晞少有才智，與紹從子含相友善，時人許以遠致，紹以為必不成器。

translations.literal: " Dai Xi of Pei was clever from youth and friendly with Shao's nephew Ji Han; people of the time promised him far-reaching success, but Shao believed he would surely fail to become a useful vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Xi of Pei was clever as a youth and close to Shao's nephew Ji Han; contemporaries predicted a brilliant career, yet Shao insisted he would never amount to anything.

sentences.zh: 晞後為司州主簿，以無行被斥，州黨稱紹有知人之明。

translations.literal: Xi later became Registrar of Si Province and was dismissed for misconduct; his provincial circle praised Shao's discernment of men.
translations.idiomatic: Xi later served as Si Province registrar until dismissed for scandalous behavior; locals then credited Shao with sound judgment of character.

sentences.zh: 轉豫章內史，以母憂，不之官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Interior Governor of Yuzhang but, owing to mourning for his mother, did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Interior Governor of Yuzhang but stayed home to mourn his mother and never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 服闋，拜徐州刺史。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he was appointed Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he received appointment as Governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時石崇為都督，性雖驕暴，而紹將之以道，崇甚親敬之。

translations.literal: At the time Shi Chong was area commander; though by nature arrogant and violent, Shao led him by principle, and Chong greatly favored and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chong was regional commander then—arrogant and harsh by nature—but Shao guided him with moral authority, and Chong came to trust and respect him deeply.

sentences.zh: 後以長子喪去職。

translations.literal: Later he left office upon the death of his eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: He later resigned when his eldest son died.

sentences.zh: 元康初，為給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuankang era he became Palace Attendant and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuankang era he was appointed Palace Attendant and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 時侍中賈謐以外戚之寵，年少居位，潘岳、杜斌等皆附托焉。

translations.literal: At the time Palace Attendant Jia Mi enjoyed favor as an imperial in-law; though young he held high rank, and Pan Yue, Du Bin, and others all attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Jia Mi then rode high as an imperial in-law; though barely grown, he wielded real power, and men such as Pan Yue and Du Bin clustered around him.

sentences.zh: 謐求交於紹，紹距而不答。

translations.literal: Mi sought friendship with Shao, but Shao kept his distance and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi courted Shao's friendship; Shao kept him at arm's length and gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 及謐誅，紹時在省，以不阿比凶族，封弋陽子，遷散騎常侍，領國子博士。

translations.literal: When Mi was executed, Shao was at the bureau; because he had not curried favor with the wicked clan, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yiyang, promoted to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and placed in charge of the doctorate of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After Mi's execution, Shao—still at his post—was rewarded for refusing to truck with that villainous clan: he received the Yiyang barony, promotion to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and concurrent charge of the Imperial Academy doctorate.

sentences.zh: 太尉、廣陵公陳准薨，太常奏諡，紹駁曰：「諡號所以垂之不朽，大行受大名，細行受細名，文武顯于功德，靈厲表於暗蔽。

translations.literal: When Grand Commandant and Duke of Guangling Chen Zhun died, the Chamberlain for Ceremonial proposed a posthumous title; Shao objected: "Posthumous titles exist to last forever—great conduct receives a great name, minor conduct a minor name; civil and martial virtue shines forth in merit, while 'spirit' and 'severe' mark hidden darkness."
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Commandant Chen Zhun, Duke of Guangling, died, the Chamberlain for Ceremonial proposed a posthumous honorific; Shao protested: titles are meant to endure—major deeds earn weighty names, slight deeds modest ones; civil and martial labels reflect true achievement, while epithets such as 'spirit' or 'severe' signal moral darkness.

sentences.zh: 自頃禮官協情，諡不依本。

translations.literal: Recently ritual officials have bent to feeling so that posthumous titles no longer follow the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the ritualists have let sentiment bend the rules, and posthumous names no longer match the facts.

sentences.zh: 准諡為過，宜諡曰繆。

translations.literal: Zhun's title is excessive; he should be styled 'Errant' (Miu).
translations.idiomatic: The proposed title for Zhun is too generous; he ought to be posthumously styled Miu—'Errant.'

sentences.zh: 」事下太常。

translations.literal: " The matter was referred to the Chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the Chamberlain for Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 時雖不從，朝廷憚焉。

translations.literal: Though the court did not follow him at the time, the officials stood in awe.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not adopt his view, yet officials took his stance seriously.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫篡位，署為侍中。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne, Shao was appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Zhao Sima Lun seized the throne, Shao was named Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 惠帝復阼，遂居其職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui resumed the throne, Shao remained in that role.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Hui was restored, Shao kept the same office.

sentences.zh: 司空張華為倫所誅，議者追理其事，欲復其爵，紹又駁曰：「臣之事君，當除煩去惑。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Hua was executed by Lun; debaters revisited the matter and wished to restore his noble rank, but Shao again objected: "A minister serves his lord by removing confusion and distraction."
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Works Zhang Hua was put to death by Lun, some argued for restoring his titles; Shao objected again: a minister's duty is to clear away trouble and delusion for his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 華歷位內外，雖粗有善事，然闔棺之責，著於遠近，兆禍始亂，華實為之。

translations.literal: Hua held posts inside and outside the court; though he had some decent deeds, the blame that closes the coffin was plain far and near—the omens that began the calamity were really his doing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua moved between palace and camp and did some good in small ways, yet his final reckoning was visible everywhere: the seeds of disaster were largely of his planting.

sentences.zh: 故鄭討幽公之亂，斫子家之棺；

translations.literal: Hence when Zheng punished the turmoil of Duke You, they hacked open Zijia's coffin;
translations.idiomatic: So Zheng, punishing Duke You of Lu's rebellion, split minister Zijia's coffin open with an axe.

sentences.zh: 魯戮隱罪，終篇貶翬。

translations.literal: Lu executed Yin for his guilt, and the classic ends by censuring Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Lu executed Guan Yin for his crime, and the Spring and Autumn closes by censuring Hui.

sentences.zh: 未忍重戮，事已弘矣，謂不宜復其爵位，理其無罪。

translations.literal: I cannot bear to urge heavier punishment; the matter is already broad enough—I say his rank should not be restored nor his innocence proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: I will not press for harsher punishment than death; the case is already settled. Restoring his titles or declaring him blameless would be wrong.

sentences.zh: 」時帝初反正，紹又上疏曰：「臣聞改前轍者則車不傾，革往弊者則政不爽。

translations.literal: " At the time the emperor had just been restored; Shao further submitted a memorial: "I have heard that those who correct the rut keep the cart from tipping; those who mend past abuses keep government sound."
translations.idiomatic: With the emperor newly restored, Shao submitted another memorial: "They say that straightening the wheel tracks keeps the carriage upright, and curing old abuses keeps government true."

sentences.zh: 太一統于元首，百司役於多士，故周文興于上，成康穆於下也。

translations.literal: The Grand Unity rests in the sovereign's head; myriad offices labor through many officers—thus King Wen rose above and Cheng and Kang were tranquil below.
translations.idiomatic: The supreme pivot sits with the ruler; every ministry depends on capable men—thus King Wen flourished on high while kings Cheng and Kang enjoyed peace below.

sentences.zh: 存不忘亡，《易》之善義；

translations.literal: To remember survival amid peril is the fine meaning of the Changes;
translations.idiomatic: The Changes teaches us to remember peril even in safety—

sentences.zh: 願陛下無忘金墉，大司馬無忘潁上，大將軍無忘黃橋，則禍亂之萌無由而兆矣。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will not forget Jinyong; the Grand Marshal will not forget Yingshang; the Grand General will not forget Huang Bridge—then the sprouts of disaster will have nowhere to arise."
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty remember the fortress at Jinyong; may the Grand Marshal remember Yingshang; may the Grand General remember Huang Bridge—then the seeds of calamity will never sprout."

sentences.zh: 齊王冏既輔政，大興第舍，驕奢滋甚，紹以書諫曰：「夏禹以卑室稱美，唐虞以茅茨顯德，豐屋蔀家，無益危亡。

translations.literal: After Prince of Qi Sima Jiong began directing affairs, he raised mansions on a grand scale and grew ever more arrogant and extravagant; Shao remonstrated in a letter: "Yu of Xia was praised for humble halls; Yao and Shun showed virtue through thatched roofs—towering houses and shady mansions do nothing to ward off ruin."
translations.idiomatic: Once Prince of Qi Sima Jiong held power, he threw up mansions and sank deeper into arrogance and luxury; Shao wrote to warn him: Yu of Xia won praise with modest halls; Yao and Shun displayed virtue through thatched roofs—grandiose dwellings buy no safety when ruin comes."

sentences.zh: 竊承毀敗太樂以廣第舍，興造功力為三王立宅，此豈今日之先急哉！

translations.literal: I hear privately that you have dismantled the Grand Music Bureau to enlarge your residence and mobilized labor to build houses for three kings—is this truly today's most urgent task!
translations.idiomatic: I hear you tore down the Directorate of Music to expand your quarters and conscripted labor to build houses for three princes—is that what matters most right now?

sentences.zh: 今大事始定，萬姓顒，咸待覆潤，宜省起造之煩，深思謙損之理。

translations.literal: The great work has barely settled; the myriad households look up, all waiting to be soaked in kindness—you should cut back on construction and deeply ponder the principle of modest yielding.
translations.idiomatic: The restoration has barely begun; the people look to you for shelter and grace—you should ease off endless building and weigh the virtue of restraint.

sentences.zh: 復主之勳不可棄矣，矢石之殆不可忘也。

translations.literal: The merit of restoring the ruler must not be cast aside; the peril of arrows and stones must not be forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Do not throw away the glory of bringing back your sovereign, nor forget how arrows and stones nearly destroyed you.

sentences.zh: 」冏雖謙順以報之，而卒不能用。

translations.literal: " Jiong answered with humility, but in the end he could not put it into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong answered politely, yet he never acted on the advice.

sentences.zh: 紹嘗詣炯諮事，遇炯宴會，召董艾、葛旗等共論時政。

translations.literal: Shao once went to Jiong to consult on business and came upon a banquet; Jiong summoned Dong Ai, Ge Qi, and others to discuss current politics together.
translations.idiomatic: Shao once went to Sima Jiong on official business and found him hosting a banquet; Jiong called in Dong Ai, Ge Qi, and others to debate affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 艾言於炯曰：「嵇侍中善於絲竹，公可令操之。

translations.literal: Ai said to Jiong: "Palace Attendant Ji is skilled on strings and pipes—my lord could have him play."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Ai said to Jiong: "Palace Attendant Ji is a master of music—you could have him perform for us."

sentences.zh: 」左右進琴，紹推不受。

translations.literal: " Attendants brought a zither; Shao declined and would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants offered a zither; Shao refused it.

sentences.zh: 冏曰：「今日為歡，卿何吝此邪！

translations.literal: Jiong said: "Today we make merry—why begrudge us this!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiong said: "We are celebrating—why so stingy with a tune?"

sentences.zh: 」紹對曰：「公匡復社稷，當軌物作則，垂之於後。

translations.literal: " Shao replied: "My lord, you have restored the altars of soil and grain; you ought to set the pattern for things and leave an example to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Shao replied: "You have rescued the altars of state; your duty is to set the standard others will follow for generations."

sentences.zh: 紹雖虛鄙，忝備常伯，腰紱冠冕，鳴玉殿省，豈可操執絲竹，以為伶人之事！

translations.literal: Though Shao is hollow and mean, I humbly serve as a permanent attendant—belt seals and court caps, jade pendants sounding in palace halls—how could I take up strings and pipes and do a player's work!
translations.idiomatic: Humble as I am, I serve among the permanent attendants—sash, seal, court crown, jade chimes in the palace offices; I cannot behave like a musician-for-hire!

sentences.zh: 若釋公服從私宴，所不敢辭也。

translations.literal: If you dismissed formal dress for a private feast, I would not presume to refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Had this been a private affair in ordinary clothes, I would not refuse.

sentences.zh: 」冏大慚。

translations.literal: " Jiong was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 艾等不自得而退。

translations.literal: Ai and the others withdrew ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Ai and the others withdrew, embarrassed.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以公事免，冏以為左司馬。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Shao was dismissed for an official matter; Jiong appointed him Left Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he lost a post over some bureaucratic matter; Jiong named him Left Adjutant.

sentences.zh: 旬日，冏被誅。

translations.literal: Within ten days Jiong was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Jiong was executed.

sentences.zh: 初，兵交，紹奔散赴宮，有持弩在東閣下者，將射之，遇有殿中將兵蕭隆，見紹姿容長者，疑非凡人，趣前拔箭，於此得免。

translations.literal: Earlier, when fighting broke out, Shao scattered and rushed to the palace; someone with a crossbow under the eastern gallery was about to shoot him when Xiao Long, a palace officer commanding troops, saw Shao's imposing stature and suspected he was no ordinary man—he rushed forward and pulled out the bolt, and thus Shao escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: When fighting first erupted, Shao raced toward the palace; a crossbowman under the eastern arcade drew a bead on him until Xiao Long, an officer on palace duty, saw Shao's commanding bearing, guessed he was someone important, darted forward and snatched the quarrel—only thus did Shao survive.

sentences.zh: 遂還滎陽舊宅。

translations.literal: He then returned to his old home in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to his old estate at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 尋徵為御史中丞，未拜，復為侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Palace Assistant Clerk of the Censorate; before he took office he again became Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned as assistant chief of the Censorate but, before taking up the post, was again named Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒、成都王穎舉兵向京都，以討長沙王乂，大駕次於城東。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Sima Yong and Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying raised troops toward the capital to strike Prince of Changsha Sima Yi; the imperial carriage halted east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hejian Sima Yong and Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying marched on the capital against Prince of Changsha Sima Yi; the imperial train halted east of the walls.

sentences.zh: 乂言於眾曰：「今日西討，欲誰為都督乎？

translations.literal: Yi said to the assembly: "Today we march west—whom do you wish as commander?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi asked the gathered officers: "For this western campaign, whom do you want as overall commander?"

sentences.zh: 」六軍之士皆曰：「願嵇侍中戮力前驅，死猶生也。

translations.literal: " The troops of the six armies said: "We wish Palace Attendant Ji to strain every nerve in the vanguard—to die would be as living."
translations.idiomatic: The men of the six armies shouted: "We want Palace Attendant Ji in the van—we would rather die beside him than live elsewhere!"

sentences.zh: 」遂拜紹使持節、平西將軍。

translations.literal: " Shao was therefore appointed commissioner bearing credentials and General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: So Shao received the credential-bearing commission and the title General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 屬乂被執，紹復為侍中。

translations.literal: When Yi was seized, Shao again became Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi was captured, Shao returned to the post of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 公王以下皆詣鄴謝罪於穎，紹等咸見廢黜，免為庶人。

translations.literal: All ranks from dukes and princes downward went to Ye to apologize to Ying; Shao and others were all cashiered and reduced to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Every prince and noble went to Ye to submit to Sima Ying; Shao and his peers were stripped of office and reduced to common status.

sentences.zh: 尋而朝廷復有北征之役，征紹，復其爵位。

translations.literal: Soon the court mounted another northern expedition and summoned Shao, restoring his noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the court launched another northern campaign, recalled Shao, and restored his titles.

sentences.zh: 紹以天子蒙塵，承詔馳詣行在所。

translations.literal: Because the Son of Heaven was in exile, Shao received the edict and galloped to the temporary residence.
translations.idiomatic: With the emperor on the run, Shao took the edict and rode hard for the imperial headquarters.

sentences.zh: 值王師敗績于蕩陰，百官及侍衛莫不散潰，唯紹儼然端冕，以身捍衛，兵交御輦，飛箭雨集，紹遂被害於帝側，血濺御服，天子深哀歎之。

translations.literal: When the royal army was routed at Dangyin, officials and guards scattered in panic—only Shao, unmoved in full court garb, shielded the ruler with his body; weapons clashed about the imperial carriage and arrows fell like rain; Shao was thus slain beside the emperor, his blood splashing the imperial robe, and the Son of Heaven mourned him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: At Dangyin the imperial army collapsed; ministers and guards fled—only Shao, erect in full court dress, threw himself between the emperor and the blades. Weapons clashed around the carriage, arrows fell like rain, and Shao died at the sovereign's side, his blood staining the imperial robe while the emperor wept over him.

sentences.zh: 及事定，左右欲浣衣，帝曰：「此嵇侍中血，勿去。」

translations.literal: When things settled, attendants wished to wash the robe; the emperor said: "This is Palace Attendant Ji's blood—do not remove it."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, servants wanted to launder the robe; the emperor said: "That is Palace Attendant Ji's blood—leave it."

sentences.zh: 初，紹之行也，侍中秦准謂曰：「今日向難，卿有佳馬否？

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shao set out, Palace Attendant Qin Zhun asked him: "Today we ride into difficulty—do you have a fine horse?"
translations.idiomatic: Before Shao departed, Palace Attendant Qin Zhun asked: "You face danger today—do you keep a good horse?"

sentences.zh: 」紹正色曰：「大駕親征，以正伐逆，理必有征無戰。

translations.literal: " Shao said sternly: "The great carriage goes on a personal expedition to punish rebellion with right—by principle there should be conquest without battle."
translations.idiomatic: Shao answered gravely: "The emperor leads the host himself to bring justice against rebels—by rights there should be submission without a fight."

sentences.zh: 若使皇輿失守，臣節有在，駿馬何為！

translations.literal: Should the imperial chariot fail, my duty as minister remains—what use is a swift horse!
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial carriage falls, a minister still owes his duty—what good would a fast horse do?

sentences.zh: 」聞者莫不歎息。

translations.literal: " None who heard failed to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who heard him drew a long breath.

sentences.zh: 及張方逼帝遷長安，河間王顒表贈紹司空，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Zhang Fang forced the emperor to move to Chang'an, Prince of Hejian Yong memorialized to posthumously award Shao Minister of Works and advance his noble rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Fang drove the court toward Chang'an, Prince of Hejian Sima Yong memorialized to posthumously name Shao Minister of Works and raise his noble rank to duke.

sentences.zh: 會帝還洛陽，事遂未行。

translations.literal: As the emperor returned to Luoyang, the matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to Luoyang, the honors were never conferred.

sentences.zh: 東海王越屯許，路經滎陽，過紹墓，哭之悲慟，刊石立碑，又表贈官爵。

translations.literal: Prince of the East Sea Sima Yue was stationed at Xu; passing through Xingyang he visited Shao's tomb, wept bitterly, had a stone inscription cut and set up, and again memorialized for posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of East Sea Sima Yue was camped at Xu; marching through Xingyang he stopped at Shao's grave, wept openly, had an inscribed stele raised, and petitioned again for posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 帝乃遣使冊贈侍中、光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，進爵為侯，賜墓田一頃，客十戶，祠以少牢。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent envoys to confer posthumously Palace Attendant, Household Grandee, with gold seal and purple ribbon, advance his rank to marquis, grant one qing of tomb land, ten households of clients, and sacrifice with the shao lao grade.
translations.idiomatic: The throne dispatched envoys to honor him posthumously as Palace Attendant and Household Grandee with gold seal and purple ribbon, raise his noble rank to marquis, grant one qing of burial land and ten dependent households, and authorize sacrifice at the shao lao level.

sentences.zh: 元帝為左丞相，承制，以紹死節事重，而贈禮未副勳德，更表贈太尉，祠乙太牢。

translations.literal: When Yuan Di was Left Chancellor of State, acting under edict, he held that Shao's martyrdom was weighty while his posthumous rewards did not match his merit; he further memorialized to posthumously award Grand Commandant and sacrifice with the tai lao grade.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuan Di served as Left Chancellor under edict, he judged Shao's martyrdom too weighty for the honors already given and memorialized again for the post of Grand Commandant and tai lao sacrifices at his shrine.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，賜諡曰忠穆，復加太牢之祠。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, he granted the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn (Zhongmu) and again added tai lao sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Di assumed the throne, he granted the posthumous epithet Zhongmu—"Loyal and Solemn"—and again authorized grand tai lao offerings.

sentences.zh: 紹誕於行己，不飾小節，然曠而有檢，通而不雜。

translations.literal: Shao was ample in self-conduct, unadorned in small points, yet open-spirited with restraint, thorough yet unmixed.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was generous in personal conduct and careless of petty polish, yet broad-minded within bounds and eclectic without losing clarity.

sentences.zh: 與從子含等五人共居，撫恤如所同生。

translations.literal: He lived with his nephews Ji Han and four others, cherishing them as if born of the same parents.
translations.idiomatic: He shared a household with five nephews including Ji Han and cared for them as his own brothers.

sentences.zh: 門人故吏思慕遺愛，行服墓次，畢三年者三十餘人。

translations.literal: More than thirty disciples and former subordinates, cherishing his kindness, wore mourning by his tomb until the three years were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Over thirty disciples and former retainers, remembering his kindness, kept mourning at his tomb until the third year ended.

sentences.zh: 長子軫，有父風，早夭。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zhen resembled his father but died young.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zhen took after him but died young.

sentences.zh: 以從孫翰襲封。

translations.literal: His great-nephew Han inherited the fief.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed to his great-nephew Han.

sentences.zh: 成帝時追述紹忠，以翰為奉朝請。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Cheng, tracing Shao's loyalty, Han was appointed Gentlemen for Court Audience.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng, recalling Shao's devotion, Han was named a court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 翰以無兄弟，自表還本宗。

translations.literal: Han, having no brothers, petitioned to return to his original lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Han, who had no brothers of his own, asked to revert to his birth line.

sentences.zh: 太元中，孝武帝詔曰：「褒德顯仁，哲王令典。

translations.literal: In the Taiyuan era, Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict: "To honor virtue and display benevolence is a wise king's proper norm."
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiyuan era, Emperor Xiaowu proclaimed: "A wise ruler's duty is to celebrate virtue and make benevolence visible."

sentences.zh: 故太尉、忠穆公執德高邈，在否彌宣，貞潔之風，義著千載。

translations.literal: The late Grand Commandant, Duke Zhongmu, held lofty integrity; in adversity he shone the brighter—his purity and steadfastness are famed across a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: The late Grand Commandant, Duke Zhongmu, bore his virtue high; in hardship it blazed all the brighter—his unstained integrity still speaks across the centuries.

sentences.zh: 每念其事，愴然傷懷。

translations.literal: Whenever I recall his deeds, my heart aches with grief.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I remember what he did, sorrow wells up anew.

sentences.zh: 忠貞之胤，蒸嘗宜遠，所以大明至節，崇獎名教。

translations.literal: The descendants of the loyal and true—their sacrifices should reach far—thus we clarify supreme integrity and exalt the teaching of names and duties.
translations.idiomatic: The line of the loyal deserves offerings long remembered; thus we proclaim the highest integrity and elevate the moral order.

sentences.zh: 可訪其宗族，襲爵主祀。

translations.literal: His clan may be sought out to inherit the noble rank and preside at sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: His kin might be found so that the title passes down and someone tends the family shrine.

sentences.zh: 」於是復以翰孫曠為弋陽侯。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Han's grandson Kuang was again made Marquis of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly Han's grandson Kuang was again invested as Marquis of Yiyang.

translations.literal: Equals sign printed in the source as an illustration placeholder.
translations.idiomatic: Woodblock edition inserts a plate marker at this point in the text.

sentences.zh: 紹從子含

translations.literal: Ji Han, Ji Shao's nephew
translations.idiomatic: Ji Han, nephew of Ji Shao

translations.literal: Second equals-sign illustration marker in the printed edition.
translations.idiomatic: Another plate divider survives from the engraved edition layout.

sentences.zh: 含字君道。

translations.literal: Han, courtesy name Jundao.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Han's courtesy name was Jundao.

sentences.zh: 祖喜，徐州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xi was Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xi had served as Governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父蕃，太子舍人。

translations.literal: His father Fan was Household Assistant to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fan had been Household Assistant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 含好學能屬文。

translations.literal: Han loved learning and could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books and could turn a polished essay.

sentences.zh: 家在鞏縣亳丘，自號亳丘子，門曰歸厚之門，室曰慎終之室。

translations.literal: His home was at Boqiu in Gong County; he styled himself Master of Boqiu; his gate was inscribed Gate of Returning to Thickness, his chamber Chamber of Being Careful to the End.
translations.idiomatic: His house stood at Boqiu in Gong County; he took the sobriquet Master of Boqiu, inscribed his gate "Gate of Returning to Thickness," and his chamber "Chamber of Honoring the Final Rites."

sentences.zh: 楚王瑋辟為掾。

translations.literal: Prince of Chu Sima Wei summoned him as aide.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chu Sima Wei appointed him as an aide.

sentences.zh: 瑋誅，坐免。

translations.literal: When Wei was executed, Han was implicated and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei was put to death, Han lost his post by association.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，除郎中。

translations.literal: Recommended as Excellent Candidate, he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as an Excellent Candidate, he received appointment as a Gentleman of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 時弘農王粹以貴公子尚主，館宇甚盛，圖莊周於室，廣集朝士，使含為之贊。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Cui of Hongnong, a noble young lord who had married a princess, had very splendid quarters; he had Zhuang Zhou pictured on his chamber and broadly gathered court gentlemen, commissioning Han to write a eulogy for it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cui of Hongnong, a wealthy young imperial son-in-law, kept lavish halls; he painted Zhuangzi on his chamber wall, hosted many courtiers, and asked Han to compose a celebratory text.

sentences.zh: 含援筆為吊文，文不加點。

translations.literal: Han took up the brush and wrote a lament text; the draft needed no blotting.
translations.idiomatic: Han seized a brush and wrote a lampoon instead—clean copy in one sitting, without a single blot.

sentences.zh: 其序曰：「帝婿王弘遠華池豐屋，廣延賢彥，圖莊生垂綸之象，記先達辭聘之事，畫真人于刻桷之室，載退士於進趣之堂，可謂托非其所，可吊不可贊也。

translations.literal: Its preface said: "The imperial son-in-law Wang Hongyuan has splendid pools and halls and broadly gathers worthy men; he has pictured Master Zhuang fishing with his line and recorded worthies of old declining appointments; he has painted the Perfected Man in a chamber with carved rafters and lodged recluses in a hall for advancing ambition—such themes may be called wrongly chosen; they may be mourned, not praised."
translations.idiomatic: The preface read: "Imperial son-in-law Wang Hongyuan boasts lavish pools and mansions and gathers eminent guests; he depicts Zhuangzi angling, memorializes elders who declined office, paints the Perfected Man under carved eaves, and installs retired scholars in a hall meant for ambition—the subjects are badly chosen: fit for lament, not praise."

sentences.zh: 」其辭曰：「邁矣莊周，天縱特放，大塊授其生，自然資其量，器虛神清，窮玄極曠。

translations.literal: " The text said: "Far indeed was Zhuang Zhou—Heaven lavished singular freedom on him; the great clod granted him life, nature endowed his capacity; his vessel was empty, his spirit clear; he plumbed mystery and reached vastness."
translations.idiomatic: The piece begins: "How distant Zhuangzi stands—Heaven let him roam free; earth gave him life and nature his breadth; hollow vessel, luminous spirit, probing the dark vast beyond."

sentences.zh: 人偽俗季，真風既散，野無訟屈之聲，朝有爭寵之歎，上下相陵，長幼失貫，於是借玄虛以助溺，引道德以自獎，戶詠恬曠之辭，家畫老莊之象。

translations.literal: Human artifice and vulgar decline—the true wind already scattered; in the wilds no sounds of litigation and grievance, at court sighs for competing favor; high and low prey on each other, elders and juniors lose proper order—thereupon they borrow empty mystery to aid drowning, cite the Way and virtue to praise themselves; every household recites words of quiet emptiness, every home paints images of Laozi and Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Artifice deepened and manners decayed—the genuine Way blew away. Countryfolk stopped airing grievances while courtiers clawed for favor; superiors and inferiors clawed one another; elders and juniors forgot their stations—then sophists grabbed Empty Mystery to excuse folly, waved Daoist slogans for self-praise, until every lane echoed hollow quietism and every wall bore Laozi and Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 今王生沈淪名利，身尚帝女，連耀三光，有出無處，池非岩石之溜，宅非茅茨之宇，馳屈產於皇衢，畫茲象其焉取！

translations.literal: Now Master Wang sinks in fame and profit; his body is yet tied to an imperial daughter; joining his gleam to sun, moon, and stars—yet he has outlet without retreat; the pool is no mountain torrent's flow, the house no thatched roof's hut; he races horses from Qu on the imperial avenues—what purpose has such a picture!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Master Wang wallows in fame and profit, rides marriage to an emperor's daughter, and basks in celestial glory—though he cannot retreat from public life; his pool is no mountain stream, his hall no thatched hut; he races Qu steeds on the capital avenues—what honest lesson does such a painting serve?

sentences.zh: 嗟乎先生，高跡何局！

translations.literal: Alas, Master—how cramped your lofty tracks!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, Master Zhuang—your lofty path reduced to this cramped stage!

sentences.zh: 生處岩岫之居，死寄雕楹之屋，托非其所，沒有餘辱，悼大道之湮晦，遂含悲而吐曲。

translations.literal: In life you dwell among cliffs and crags; in death you lodge beneath carved pillars—you have entrusted yourself to the wrong place—death still brings lingering shame. Grieving the obscuring of the Great Way, I therefore hold sorrow and pour forth this song.
translations.idiomatic: Alive you belonged among cliffs; dead you are staged beneath carved pillars—you lie where you never ought to be, and shame survives your bones. Mourning how the Great Way has dimmed, I sound this mournful lay."

sentences.zh: 」粹有愧色。

translations.literal: " Cui showed a shamefaced look.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cui colored with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏辟為征西參軍，襲爵武昌鄉侯。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Sima Jiong summoned him as adjutant on the western expedition and he inherited the village marquisate of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Sima Jiong appointed him adjutant on the western campaign, and he inherited the village marquisate at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 長沙王乂召為驃騎記室督、尚書郎。

translations.literal: Prince of Changsha Sima Yi summoned him as recorder-in-chief to the chief commander and Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Changsha Sima Yi appointed him recorder-in-chief to the chief commander and Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乂與成都王穎交戰，穎軍轉盛，尚書郎旦出督戰，夜還理事。

translations.literal: Yi fought Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying; Ying's army grew stronger; the Secretariat gentlemen went out at dawn to oversee battle and returned at night to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi clashed with Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying, Ying's forces gained ground; the Secretariat gentlemen rode out at dawn to supervise the fighting and returned after dark to manage paperwork.

sentences.zh: 含言於乂曰：「昔魏武每有軍事，增置掾屬。

translations.literal: Han said to Yi: "In old days whenever Wu of Wei had military affairs, he added aides and staff."
translations.idiomatic: Han urged Yi: "Whenever Emperor Wu of Wei faced war, he expanded aide posts."

sentences.zh: 青龍二年，尚書令陳矯以有軍務，亦奏增郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qinglong, Director of the Secretariat Chen Jiao, because there were military matters, also memorialized to add gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: In Qinglong 2, Director of the Secretariat Chen Jiao, citing military business, likewise petitioned for added Secretariat gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 今奸逆四逼，王路擁塞，倒懸之急，不復過此。

translations.literal: Now treason presses from four sides; the royal road is blocked; the urgency of hanging upside down could not be greater.
translations.idiomatic: Today rebels ring us on every side; the imperial highways clog; we hang by our heels—nothing could be more urgent.

sentences.zh: 但居曹理事，尚須增郎，況今都官中騎三曹晝出督戰，夜還理事，一人兩役，內外廢乏。

translations.literal: Yet merely sitting in headquarters handling business still requires added gentlemen—how much more now when the Capital Bureau, Palace Bureau, and Cavalry Bureau go out by day to oversee battle and return by night to handle affairs—one man bearing two duties, inner and outer alike exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Stationery offices still need extra hands in quiet times—how much more when the Capital, Palace, and Cavalry sections march out by day to direct combat and draft orders by night; one officer pulling double duty exhausts both camp and capital.

sentences.zh: 含謂今有十萬人，都督各有主帥，推轂授綏，委付大將，不宜復令台僚雜與其間。

translations.literal: Han holds that with one hundred thousand men, each command has its commander; push the carriage and hand the reins—entrust it to a great general; you should not again let terrace aides mix among them.
translations.idiomatic: Han argues that with a hundred thousand troops under distinct commanders—each lieutenant invested with drum and reins—a chief general should hold the line; secretariat aides ought not clutter the chain of command.

sentences.zh: 」乂從之，乃增郎及令史。

translations.literal: " Yi followed him and added gentlemen and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Yi agreed and expanded the Secretariat rolls with added gentlemen and clerks.

sentences.zh: 懷帝為撫軍將軍，以含為從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai was General Who Pacifies the Army, he appointed Han as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: While still General Who Pacifies the Army, Emperor Huai named Han his administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 惠帝北征，轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui campaigned north, Han was transferred to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Hui's northern expedition Han moved to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及蕩陰之敗，含走歸滎陽。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Dangyin, Han fled back to Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the rout at Dangyin he bolted home to Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 永興初，除太弟中庶子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongxing era he was appointed Palace Cadet to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongxing he received appointment as Palace Cadet to the imperial heir.

sentences.zh: 西道阻閡，未得應召。

translations.literal: The western route was blocked; he could not answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Western roads were closed; he could not reach court.

sentences.zh: 范陽王虓為征南將軍，屯許昌，復以含為從事中郎。

translations.literal: Prince of Fanyang Sima Xiao was General Who Campaigns South, stationed at Xuchang, and again appointed Han as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Fanyang Sima Xiao, General Who Campaigns South and stationed at Xuchang, again took Han on as administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 尋授振威將軍、襄城太守。

translations.literal: Shortly he was granted General Who Rouses Might and Administrator of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received the rank General Who Rouses Might and the magistracy of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 虓為劉喬所破，含奔鎮南將軍劉弘于襄陽，弘待以上賓之禮。

translations.literal: When Xiao was defeated by Liu Qiao, Han fled to Regional Commander Who Guards the South Liu Hong at Xiangyang; Hong treated him as an honored guest.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Qiao routed Xiao, Han fled to Regional Commander Liu Hong at Xiangyang, who received him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 含性通敏，好薦達才賢，常欲崇趙武之諡，加臧文之罪。

translations.literal: Han was by nature quick and keen and enjoyed recommending talented worthies; he always wished to elevate the posthumous title of Zhao Wu and add to the guilt of Zang Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Han was quick-witted and loved lifting worthy men; he often argued for honoring Zhao Wu's posthumous name and indicting Zang Wenzhong—historical precedents for reward and blame.

sentences.zh: 屬陳敏作亂，江揚震盪，南越險遠，而廣州刺史王毅病卒，弘表含為平越中郎將、廣州刺史、假節。

translations.literal: When Chen Min rebelled, the Yangzi and Huai regions shook; the far south was perilous and remote; Inspector of Guangzhou Wang Yi died of illness—Hong memorialized Han as General Who Pacifies the Yue, Inspector of Guangzhou, with credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min's revolt convulsed the south; Guangzhou lay distant and perilous; when Inspector Wang Yi died in office, Liu Hong petitioned to make Han General Who Pacifies the Yue, Inspector of Guangzhou, with credential staff.

sentences.zh: 未發，會弘卒，時或欲留含領刑州。

translations.literal: Before he set out, Hong died; some then wished to retain Han to administer Xing Province (graphical error in the text for Jing Province).
translations.idiomatic: Before Han could depart, Liu Hong died; some officials wanted him to stay on and govern Jing Province instead—the manuscript miswrites the province name.

sentences.zh: 含性剛躁，素與弘司馬郭勱有隙，勱疑含將為己害，夜掩殺之，時年四十四。

translations.literal: Han was by nature harsh and impatient and had long been at odds with Hong's army aide Guo Mai; Mai suspected Han would harm him and by night attacked and killed him—he was forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Han was brittle and quick-tempered and had long feuded with Liu Hong's adjutant Guo Mai; Mai feared Han would murder him and struck first by night—Han died at forty-four.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，諡曰憲。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai took the throne, Han was posthumously titled Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huai ascended the throne, Han received the posthumous epithet Xian—"Lawful."

sentences.zh: 王豹

translations.literal: Wang Bao
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao

sentences.zh: 王豹，順陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Bao was a man of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao came from Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 少而抗直。

translations.literal: From youth he was upright and blunt.
translations.idiomatic: Even young he was blunt and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 初為豫州別駕，齊王冏為大司馬，以豹為主簿。

translations.literal: At first he was Regional Assistant of Yu Province; when Prince of Qi Sima Jiong was Grand Marshal, he appointed Bao chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Ye Province's chief clerk; when Prince of Qi Sima Jiong served as Grand Marshal, Bao became his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 冏驕縱，失天下心，豹致箋於冏曰：

translations.literal: Jiong was arrogant and unrestrained and lost the hearts of the realm; Bao sent Jiong a memorandum saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jiong grew arrogant and forfeited popular loyalty; Bao submitted a long memorandum opening thus:

sentences.zh: :豹聞王臣蹇蹇，匪躬之故，將以安主定時，保存社稷者也。

translations.literal: :Bao has heard that royal ministers who labor tirelessly do so not for themselves alone—they aim to secure the ruler, settle the age, and preserve the altars.
translations.idiomatic: "Bao has heard that ministers who toil without rest do so not for private ends—they mean to steady the sovereign, quiet the times, and preserve the altars of soil and grain."

sentences.zh: 是以為人臣而欺其君者，刑罰不足以為誅；

translations.literal: Therefore for a subject to deceive his lord—punishments are not enough to execute him;
translations.idiomatic: Thus a subject who deceives his prince cannot be punished enough by mere law—

sentences.zh: 為人主而逆其諫者，靈厲不足以為諡。

translations.literal: for a ruler to reject remonstrance—'spirit' and 'severe' are not enough for his posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: and a ruler who spurns honest counsel deserves worse than posthumous epithets like Ling or Li.

sentences.zh: 伏惟明公虛心下士，開懷納善，款誠以著，而逆耳之言未入於聽。

translations.literal: I reflect that though you, sir, empty your mind for inferiors and open your breast to accept good counsel, your sincere devotion is evident yet unwelcome words do not enter your hearing.
translations.idiomatic: You incline your mind toward humble advisers and open your heart to good counsel—your loyalty shines clear—yet words that grate still fail to reach your ears.

sentences.zh: 豹伏思晉政漸缺，始自元康以來，宰相在位，未有一人獲終，乃事勢使然，未為輒有不善也。

translations.literal: Bao reflects that Jin government has gradually failed since the Yuankang era; not one chief minister in office has met a natural end—it is the trend of circumstances, not necessarily that each was unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Bao reflects that Jin governance has frayed since Yuankang: no chief minister has died in office of natural causes—not always because they were wicked, but because the times made it so.

sentences.zh: 今公克平禍亂，安國定家，故復因前傾敗之法，尋中間覆車之軌，欲冀長存，非所敢聞。

translations.literal: Now you have crushed rebellion and settled the state and household—yet if you again adopt the ways that brought earlier ruin and follow the overturned cart's middle rut, hoping thereby for lasting preservation—that is not a prospect I dare endorse.
translations.idiomatic: You have crushed rebellion and restored the realm—yet if you cling to the habits that ruined prior regimes and ride the same rut that flipped the cart while expecting to endure forever, that is an outcome I cannot bring myself to contemplate.

sentences.zh: 今河間樹根于關右，成都盤桓于舊魏，新野大封于江漢，三面貴王，各以方剛強盛，並典戎馬，處險害之地。

translations.literal: Now Prince of Hejian has rooted himself west of the pass, Prince of Chengdu lingers in old Wei territory, Prince of Xinye holds broad feoffs along the Yangzi and Han—the three royal princes are strong in their regions, each commanding troops and occupying perilous ground.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hejian has sunk roots west of the passes; Prince of Chengdu holds sway in the old Wei heartland; Prince of Xinye commands vast fiefs along the Han—these three royal uncles are powerful in their quarters, each leading armies on dangerous ground.

sentences.zh: 且明公興義討逆，功蓋天下，聖德光茂，名震當世。

translations.literal: Moreover you, sir, raised loyal troops against rebels; your merit overshadows the realm, your sagely virtue shines abundant, your name shakes the age.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover you raised righteous armies against traitors; your merit overshadows the realm, your virtue dazzles, your name shakes the age.

sentences.zh: 今以難賞之功，挾震主之威，獨據京都，專執大權，進則亢龍有悔，退則蒺藜生庭，冀此求安，未知其福。

translations.literal: Now with merit hard to reward you wield awe that bends the ruler; you alone occupy the capital and monopolize great power—advance and the soaring dragon knows regret; withdraw and tribulus grows in your courtyard—seeking safety thus, I do not know its blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Your achievements outstrip any reward; your prestige overshadows the throne; you alone hold the capital and grasp supreme authority—press forward and you tread the dragon's sixth line—regret; step back and brambles choke your courtyard. To seek safety there—I see little fortune in it.

sentences.zh: 敢以淺見，陳寫愚情。

translations.literal: I dare offer my shallow view and set forth my foolish sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Forgive my humble sight—I lay out my earnest though blunt counsel.

sentences.zh: :昔武王伐紂，封建諸侯為二伯，自陝以東，周公主之，自陝以西，召公主之。

translations.literal: :In antiquity King Wu attacked Zhou and enfeoffed the feudal lords as two elders—east of Shan the Duke of Zhou ruled them, west of Shan the Duke of Shao ruled them.
translations.idiomatic: "When King Wu overthrew Shang, he arrayed the feudal lords as two paramount lords: east of Mount Shan the Duke of Zhou held sway, west of Mount Shan the Duke of Shao."

sentences.zh: 及至其末，霸國之世，不過數州之地，四海強兵不敢入窺九鼎，所以然者，天下習於所奉故也。

translations.literal: Down to its late age of hegemon states they held only several provinces' ground; strong armies of the four seas dared not covet the nine tripods—the reason was that all under heaven were habituated to whom they served.
translations.idiomatic: Later hegemonic kingdoms controlled only a few provinces, yet no army in the realm dared covet the Nine Tripods—because people everywhere had grown used to whom they obeyed.

sentences.zh: 今誠能尊用周法，以成都為北州伯，統河北之王侯，明公為南州伯，以攝南土之官長，各因本職，出居其方，樹德於外，盡忠於內，歲終率所領而貢于朝，簡良才，命賢俊，以為天子百官，則四海長寧，萬國幸甚，明公之德當與周召同其至美，危敗路塞，社稷可保。

translations.literal: Now if we truly could honor and employ the Zhou model—make Chengdu the elder of the northern provinces to oversee the princes north of the Yellow River; make you, sir, elder of the southern provinces to gather the long officials of the southern soil—each according to original duty going out to dwell in his quarter, planting virtue abroad and showing loyalty within, at year's end leading what they govern to present tribute at court, selecting fine talent and ordering worthy men to form the Son of Heaven's hundred offices—then the four seas would be ever calm and all states greatly fortunate; your virtue would match the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao at their finest; the road to peril would be blocked and the altars preserved.
translations.idiomatic: If we truly revived Zhou practice—making Chengdu lord of the northern quarter over the Hebei princes while you, sir, ruled the southern quarter over southern officials—each settling in his domain, winning virtue abroad and loyalty at home, rendering yearly tribute and staffing the Son of Heaven's ministries with chosen talent—the realm would rest secure and every state rejoice; your virtue would rival the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao; ruin would find no road and the altars would endure.

sentences.zh: 顧明公思高祖納婁敬之策，悟張良履足之謀，遠臨深之危，保泰山之安。

translations.literal: I pray you will ponder Gaozu's acceptance of Lou Jing's plan and Zhang Liang's lesson from treading on his foot—avoid the peril of standing over a deep abyss and keep Mount Tai's peace.
translations.idiomatic: Think how Emperor Gaozu took Lou Jing's counsel and grasped Zhang Liang's warning when he trod on his lord's foot—shun the brink of the abyss and stand firm as Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 若合聖思，宛許可都也。

translations.literal: If it matches sagely intent, Wan might serve as capital.
translations.idiomatic: If it suits your intent, Wan might serve as capital.

sentences.zh: 書入，無報，豹重箋曰：

translations.literal: When the letter went in there was no reply; Bao sent another memorandum:
translations.idiomatic: The memorial drew no answer; Bao wrote again:

sentences.zh: :豹書御已來，十有二日，而聖旨高遠，未垂采察，不賜一字之令，不敕可否之宜。

translations.literal: :Since Bao's letter reached the throne twelve days have passed, yet the sagely intent remains lofty and distant—no glance of approval, not one word of command, no ruling on whether it may or may not.
translations.idiomatic: "Twelve days have passed since my memorial reached you, yet heaven-high silence—no scrap of guidance, no verdict on whether to adopt or reject it.

sentences.zh: 蓋霸王之神寶，安危之秘術，不可須臾而忽者也。

translations.literal: This is the divine treasure of hegemon kings, the secret art of safety and peril—it cannot be neglected even for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: These are the instruments by which hegemons rise and the secrets of survival—none may neglect them for an instant.

sentences.zh: 伏思明公挾大功，抱大名，懷大德，執大權，此四大者，域中所不能容，賢聖所以戰戰兢兢，日昃不暇食，雖休勿休者也。

translations.literal: I reflect that you, sir, embrace great merit, great name, great virtue, and great power—these four the realm cannot contain; hence worthies and sages tremble with care, the sun past noon yet no leisure to eat—though there be rest, they do not rest.
translations.idiomatic: You bear towering merit, fame, virtue, and power together—the world scarce holds such weight; that is why even sages tremble, skip meals past noon, and refuse ease while crisis lingers.

sentences.zh: 昔周公以武王為兄，成王為君，伐紂有功，以親輔政，執德弘深，聖思博遠，至忠至仁，至孝至敬。

translations.literal: In old days the Duke of Zhou had King Wu as elder brother and King Cheng as lord; he punished Zhou with merit and assisted government by kin; his virtue ran deep, his sagely thought broad—supreme loyalty, supreme humaneness, supreme filiality, supreme reverence.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou served King Wu as brother and King Cheng as sovereign; he destroyed Shang and then guided the boy king—virtue profound, vision vast, loyalty, humaneness, filial piety, and reverence without peer.

sentences.zh: 而攝事之日，四國流言，離主出奔，居東三年，賴風雨之變，成王感悟。

translations.literal: Yet while administering affairs, rumor spread through four states; he left the ruler and fled east three years—until wind and rain brought omens and King Cheng came to understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Yet while regent he faced rumors across four domains, fled east from court for three years, and only omens of wind and thunder woke King Cheng to the truth.

sentences.zh: 若不遭皇天之應，神人之察，恐公旦之禍未知所限也。

translations.literal: Had Heaven's response and insight of gods and men not come, the disaster of the Duke of Zhou might have known no limit.
translations.idiomatic: Without Heaven's answering portent and the gods' scrutiny, the Duke of Zhou might never have escaped calamity.

sentences.zh: 至於執政，猶與召公分陝為伯。

translations.literal: Even when holding power, he still divided Shan with the Duke of Shao as elders.
translations.idiomatic: Even in power he split Mount Shan with the Duke of Shao and ruled only half the realm.

sentences.zh: 今明公自視功德孰如周公。

translations.literal: Now consider how your merit and virtue compare with the Duke of Zhou's.
translations.idiomatic: Consider how your merit stacks against the Duke of Zhou's.

sentences.zh: 且元康以來，宰相之患，危機竊發，不及容思，密禍潛起，輒在呼噏，豈復晏然得全生計！

translations.literal: Moreover since Yuankang, the peril of chief ministers—crises burst forth before one could think; hidden calamities arose between breaths—how could one stay peacefully and preserve life!
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuankang, chief ministers have faced crises that strike before thought—the disaster arrives between breaths; how can anyone stay comfortably alive?

sentences.zh: 前鑒不遠，公所親見也。

translations.literal: The mirror of the past is not far—it is what you yourself have seen.
translations.idiomatic: Recent precedent lies before your eyes.

sentences.zh: 君子不有遠慮，必有近憂，憂至乃悟，悔無所及也。

translations.literal: If the gentleman lacks far-reaching thought, he will have near sorrow; when sorrow arrives it is too late for regret.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman without long sight invites immediate grief; when grief arrives, regret is useless.

sentences.zh: :今若從豹此策，皆遣王侯之國，北與成都分河為伯，成都在鄴，明公都宛，寬方千里，以與圻內侯伯子男小大相率，結好要盟，同獎皇家；

translations.literal: :Now if you follow Bao's plan—send all the royal princes to their fiefs; northward with Chengdu divide at the river as elders—Chengdu at Ye, you, sir, at Wan—a breadth of a thousand li; let marquises, earls, and barons great and small within the domains join in leagues of alliance and together aid the royal house;
translations.idiomatic: "If you adopt my plan—dispatch every prince to his fief; north of the river partner Chengdu as co-elder while Chengdu stays at Ye and you hold Wan—a thousand-li belt—binding inner-domain nobles in treaties that jointly shield the throne—"

sentences.zh: 貢御之法，一如周典。

translations.literal: tribute and audience follow the Zhou statutes.
translations.idiomatic: tribute and audience would follow Zhou precedent.

sentences.zh: 若合聖規，可先旨與成都共論。

translations.literal: If it matches sagely rule, you may first communicate intent with Chengdu to discuss together.
translations.idiomatic: If this suits your design, sound out Chengdu first.

sentences.zh: 雖以小才，願備行人。

translations.literal: Though my talent is slight, I wish to serve as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Humble as my talents are, I volunteer as envoy.

sentences.zh: 昔廝養，燕趙之微者耳，百里奚，秦楚之商人也，一開其說，兩國以寧。

translations.literal: Of old grooms were the meanest in Yan and Zhao; Baili Xi was a merchant of Qin and Chu—once they opened their persuasion, both states were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Stableboys were the lowest rungs in Yan and Zhao; Baili Xi peddled cattle between Qin and Chu—yet their words once heard brought peace to whole realms.

sentences.zh: 況豹雖陋，大州之綱紀，加明公起事險難之主簿也。

translations.literal: How much more Bao, though mean, was chief clerk for a great province and your chief clerk when you raised the enterprise in peril.
translations.idiomatic: I am chief clerk of a great province and served as your chief clerk when you launched this perilous undertaking.

sentences.zh: 故身雖輕，其言未必否也。

translations.literal: Thus though my person is light, my words may not be worthless.
translations.idiomatic: My person carries little weight; my counsel may still merit hearing.

sentences.zh: 冏令曰：「得前後白事，具意，輒別思量也。

translations.literal: Jiong ordered: "I have received your successive reports in full; I will consider them separately.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong replied: "I have your successive memorials in full; I will weigh them separately."

sentences.zh: 」會長沙王乂至，於冏案上見豹箋，謂冏曰：「小子離間骨肉，何不銅駝下打殺！

translations.literal: " When Prince of Changsha Sima Yi arrived, he saw Bao's memorandum on Jiong's desk and said to Jiong: "This boy sows discord among flesh and blood—why not beat him to death under the bronze camels!"
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Changsha Sima Yi arrived, he spotted Bao's paper on Jiong's desk and snarled: "This whelp sows strife in the royal family—beat him to death under the bronze camels!"

sentences.zh: 」冏既不能嘉豹之策，遂納乂言，乃奏豹曰：「臣忿奸凶肆逆，皇祚顛墜，與成都、長沙、新野共興義兵，安復社稷，唯欲戮力皇家，與親親宗室腹心從事，此臣夙夜自誓，無負神明。

translations.literal: " Jiong could not embrace Bao's plan; he accepted Yi's words and therefore memorialized concerning Bao: "Your subject resents how villains ran riot and the imperial fortune toppled; with Chengdu, Changsha, and Xinyue he jointly raised loyal troops to restore the altars—my sole wish is to strain every nerve for the royal house and work heart to heart with close imperial kin—this is what your subject swears day and night, not betraying the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong spurned Bao's advice and took Yi's bait, memorializing: "Your servant burns as traitors overturn heaven; with Chengdu, Changsha, and Xinyue I raised righteous armies to heal the altars—my vow night and day is to exhaust myself for the throne alongside true kinsmen—may the spirits witness me."

sentences.zh: 而主簿王豹比有白事，敢造異端，謂臣忝備宰相，必遘危害，慮在一旦，不祥之聲可蹻足而待，欲臣與成都分陝為伯，盡出籓王。

translations.literal: Yet chief clerk Wang Bao has repeatedly submitted reports daring to craft strange heterodoxy, claiming your subject, shamefully filling the role of chief minister, is sure to meet harm and that peril waits within the day—inauspicious cries may arrive as soon as one lifts a heel—wishing your subject with Chengdu to divide Shan as elders and send out all the feudal princes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet chief clerk Wang Bao keeps forwarding heterodox schemes—claiming this minister, unworthy though I am of the chancellorship, faces doom within days and ill omens before we lift a foot—demanding that I split the realm with Chengdu like the ancient elders and banish every prince to his fief."

sentences.zh: 上誣聖朝鑒御之威，下長妖惑，疑阻眾心，噂背憎，巧賣兩端，訕上謗下，讒內間外，遘惡導奸，坐生猜嫌。

translations.literal: Above he slanders the sagely court's awesome governance; below he fosters weird delusion, doubts and blocks the host of hearts—backbiting and hatred; he craftily sells to both sides, mocks above and slanders below, slanders within and estranges without—encountering evil and guiding villainy, sitting and breeding suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: He traduces imperial majesty above while sowing panic below; he sets minds doubting and breeds whispered hatred; he plays both ends, mocks superiors and baits inferiors, slanders court and alienates the regions—drawing villains together until suspicion festers."

sentences.zh: 昔孔丘匡魯，乃誅少正；

translations.literal: In old days Confucius restored Lu and thus executed Shaozheng Mao;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius restored Lu by executing Shaozheng Mao—"

sentences.zh: 子產相鄭，先戮鄧析，誠以交亂名實，若趙高詭怪之類也。

translations.literal: Zichan served Zheng as minister and first executed Deng Xi—truly because they confused name with reality, like Zhao Gao's deceitful sort.
translations.idiomatic: Zichan governed Zheng and executed Deng Xi first—both struck down men who twisted name and fact like Zhao Gao's breed."

sentences.zh: 豹為臣不忠不順不義，輒敕都街考竟，以明邪正。

translations.literal: Bao as a subject was disloyal, unfilial, and unjust—your subject orders him interrogated to death in the capital avenue to clarify evil and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao is disloyal, unfilial, unjust—I order him beaten to death in the capital street to mark the line between treason and right."

sentences.zh: 」豹將死，曰：「懸吾頭大司馬門，見兵之攻齊也。

translations.literal: " As Bao was about to die he said: "Hang my head at the Grand Marshal's gate—watch the armies attack Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death Bao said: "Hang my head on the Grand Marshal's gate—you will see armies march against Qi."

sentences.zh: 」眾庶冤之。

translations.literal: " The common people thought him wronged.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd counted him wronged.

sentences.zh: 俄而冏敗。

translations.literal: Soon Jiong was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Sima Jiong fell.

sentences.zh: 劉沈

translations.literal: Liu Shen
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen

sentences.zh: 劉沈，字道真，燕國薊人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shen, courtesy name Daozhen, was a man of Ji in the state of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen, courtesy name Daozhen, came from Ji in Yan.

sentences.zh: 世為北州名族。

translations.literal: For generations his clan was a distinguished house of the northern provinces.
translations.idiomatic: His clan ranked among the north's great families for generations.

sentences.zh: 少仕州郡，博學好古。

translations.literal: In youth he served in provincial posts; he was broadly learned and loved antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Youth brought minor provincial posts; he read widely and revered antiquity.

sentences.zh: 太保衛瓘辟為掾，領本邑大中正。

translations.literal: Grand Mentor Wei Guan summoned him as aide and assigned him concurrent duty as senior rectifier for his native district.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Mentor Wei Guan took him on as an aide and put him in charge of local personnel appraisal as senior rectifier.

sentences.zh: 敦儒道，愛賢能，進霍原為二品，及申理張華，皆辭旨明峻，為當時所稱。

translations.literal: He honored Confucian teaching and loved worthy talent; advancing Huo Yuan to the second rank and arguing Zhang Hua's case—all were marked by bright, stern wording and praised by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: He championed scholarship, prized talent, promoted Huo Yuan to the second grade, and defended Zhang Hua—each memorial lucid and uncompromising, earning wide acclaim.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏輔政，引為左長史，遷侍中。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Sima Jiong directed affairs, he summoned Shen as Left Senior Clerk and promoted him to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Sima Jiong, while directing government, brought Liu Shen in as Left Senior Clerk and soon promoted him to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 于時李流亂蜀，詔沈以侍中、假節，統益州刺史羅尚、梁州刺史許雄等以討流。

translations.literal: At that time Li Liu rebelled in Shu; an edict appointed Shen as Palace Attendant with credential staff to oversee Inspector of Yi Province Luo Shang, Inspector of Liang Province Xu Xiong, and others to strike Liu.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Liu ravaged Shu, the throne named Liu Shen Palace Attendant with credential staff to coordinate Luo Shang of Yi Province, Xu Xiong of Liang Province, and others against him.

sentences.zh: 行次長安，河間王顒請留沉為軍司，遣席薳代之。

translations.literal: Marching, he halted at Chang'an; Prince of Hejian Yong requested to retain Shen as army marshal and sent Xi Yuan to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: His march paused at Chang'an; Prince of Hejian Sima Yong asked to keep Liu Shen as army marshal and dispatched Xi Yuan to replace him on campaign.

sentences.zh: 後領雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he concurrently served as Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He later added concurrent duty as Inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 及張昌作亂，詔顒遣沉將州兵萬人並征西府五千人，自藍田關以討之，顒不奉詔。

translations.literal: When Zhang Chang rebelled, an edict ordered Yong to send Shen leading ten thousand provincial troops plus five thousand from the western expedition headquarters through Lantian Pass to attack him; Yong did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chang rose, an edict told Yong to send Liu Shen with ten thousand Yong troops and five thousand western expedition troops through Lantian Pass—Yong ignored it.

sentences.zh: 沉自領州兵至藍田，顒又逼奪其眾。

translations.literal: Shen himself led provincial troops to Lantian; Yong again pressed and seized his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen drove the provincial army to Lantian anyway; Yong seized those troops from him.

sentences.zh: 長沙王乂命沉將武吏四百人還州。

translations.literal: Prince of Changsha Yi ordered Shen to lead four hundred martial clerks back to the province.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Changsha Sima Yi ordered Liu Shen to march four hundred armed clerks back to Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 張方既逼京都，王師屢敗，王瑚、祖逖言於乂曰：「劉沈忠義果毅，雍州兵力足制河間，宜啟上詔與沈，使發兵襲顒，顒窘急，必召張方以自救，此計之良也。

translations.literal: Once Zhang Fang threatened the capital and the royal army repeatedly lost, Wang Hu and Zu Ti said to Yi: "Liu Shen is loyal, righteous, resolute, and daring; Yong Province's military strength is enough to control Hejian—you should memorialize the throne to issue an edict to Shen ordering him to raise troops and strike Yong; Yong, embarrassed and pressed, is sure to summon Zhang Fang to rescue himself—this is an excellent plan."
translations.idiomatic: With Zhang Fang threatening Luoyang and imperial armies failing, Wang Hu and Zu Ti urged Sima Yi: "Liu Shen is loyal and bold; Yong Province can pin Prince of Hejian—petition the emperor to order Shen to strike Yong; Yong, desperate, will recall Zhang Fang—that breaks the siege."

sentences.zh: 」乂從之。

translations.literal: " Yi followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi agreed.

sentences.zh: 沈奉詔馳檄四境，合七郡之眾及守防諸軍、塢壁甲士萬餘人，以安定太守衛博、新平太守張光、安定功曹皇甫澹為先登，襲長安。

translations.literal: Shen received the edict and galloped proclamations through the four borders, assembling the hosts of seven counties together with garrison defenders and fort warriors—over ten thousand—and with Administrator of Anding Wei Bo, Administrator of Xinping Zhang Guang, and merit evaluator Huangfu Dan of Anding as van bearers, attacked Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen rode the edict to rally seven counties, garrisons, and fortress troops—more than ten thousand—then struck Chang'an with Wei Bo of Anding, Zhang Guang of Xinping, and Huangfu Dan leading the van.

sentences.zh: 顒時頓于鄭縣之高平亭，為東軍聲援，聞沈兵起，還鎮渭城，遣督護虞夔率步騎萬餘人逆沈於好畤。

translations.literal: Yong at that time was halted at Gaoping Pavilion in Zheng County as eastern-army support; hearing Shen's troops had risen, he returned to guard Weicheng and sent Protector Yu Kui with over ten thousand infantry and cavalry to oppose Shen at Haozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong had camped at Gaoping Pavilion to screen eastern reinforcements; hearing Liu Shen move, he pulled back to Weicheng and sent Yu Kui with ten thousand horse and foot to intercept Shen at Haozhi.

sentences.zh: 接戰，夔眾敗，顒大懼，退入長安，果急呼張方。

translations.literal: They engaged in battle; Kui's host was defeated; Yong was greatly afraid and withdrew into Chang'an, urgently summoning Zhang Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Kui lost the engagement; Yong fled into Chang'an in panic and screamed for Zhang Fang.

sentences.zh: 沈渡渭而壘，顒每遣兵出鬥，輒不利，沈乘勝攻之，使澹、博以精甲五千，從長安門而入，力戰至顒帳下。

translations.literal: Shen crossed the Wei and built ramparts; Yong repeatedly sent troops out to fight but consistently failed; Shen exploited victory to attack him, ordering Dan and Bo with five thousand picked armored troops to enter through Chang'an Gate and fight fiercely to Yong's command tent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen crossed the Wei and walled up; Yong's sallies failed again and again—Shen pressed the advantage, sending Huangfu Dan and Wei Bo with five thousand elite armored men through Chang'an Gate to fight through to Yong's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 沈軍來遲，顒軍見澹等無繼，氣益倍。

translations.literal: Shen's army arrived late; Yong's troops saw Dan and others had no reinforcements and their morale doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's main body arrived late; Yong's men saw Dan had no backup and doubled their fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 馮翊太守張輔率眾救顒，橫擊之，大戰於府門，博父子皆死之，澹又被擒。

translations.literal: Administrator of Fengyi Zhang Fu led a host to rescue Yong and struck them sideways; they fought a great battle at the headquarters gate—Bo and his son both died in it, and Dan was also captured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu of Fengyi slammed into Shen's flank before Yong's yamen—Wei Bo and his son died there; Huangfu Dan was taken.

sentences.zh: 顒奇澹壯勇，將活之。

translations.literal: Yong marveled at Dan's bravery and wished to spare him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong admired Dan's courage and meant to spare him.

sentences.zh: 澹不為之屈，於是見殺。

translations.literal: Dan would not yield and was therefore executed.
translations.idiomatic: Dan refused to bend, so Yong executed him.

sentences.zh: 沈軍遂敗，率余卒屯于故營。

translations.literal: Shen's army was thus defeated; he led surviving troops to camp at the old stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's line collapsed; he gathered survivors at the old camp.

sentences.zh: 張方遣其將敦偉夜至，沈軍大驚而潰，與麾下百餘人南遁，為陳倉令所執。

translations.literal: Zhang Fang sent his general Dun Wei by night; Shen's army panicked and scattered; with over a hundred followers he fled south and was seized by the magistrate of Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang's officer Dun Wei struck by night; Shen's men broke and fled—he escaped south with a hundred riders until the Chencang magistrate seized him.

sentences.zh: 沈謂顒曰：「夫知己之顧輕，在三之節重，不可違君父之詔，量強弱以苟全。

translations.literal: Shen said to Yong: "Though favor from a confidant may be light, the obligation of the three bonds weighs heavily—I may not disobey father and lord's edicts nor gauge strength and weakness to preserve myself cheaply."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen told Yong: "Private kindness weighs little beside the three great bonds—I cannot defy sovereign and father to save myself by calculating odds."

sentences.zh: 投袂之日，期之必死，菹醢之戮，甘之如薺。

translations.literal: The day I cast aside my sleeve I fixed my heart on death—pickling and mincing punishment I would relish like shepherd's purse.
translations.idiomatic: The day I raised arms I accepted death—mincing and saucing would taste to me like spring greens."

sentences.zh: 」辭義慷慨，見者哀之。

translations.literal: " His words were righteous and stirring; those who saw pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke with blazing conviction; onlookers wept for him.

sentences.zh: 顒怒，鞭之而後腰斬。

translations.literal: Yong angrily flogged him and then cut him in two at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had him flogged, then cut in half at the waist.

sentences.zh: 有識者以顒干上犯順，虐害忠義，知其滅亡不久也。

translations.literal: Knowing men considered that Yong had offended superiors and violated propriety and cruelly harmed loyalty and righteousness—they knew his destruction would come soon.
translations.idiomatic: Thoughtful observers saw Yong defying heaven and torturing loyal men—they knew he would not last.

sentences.zh: 麴允

translations.literal: Qu Yun
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun

sentences.zh: 麴允，金城人也。

translations.literal: Qu Yun was a man of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun came from Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 與游氏世為豪族，西州為之語曰：「麴與游，牛羊不數頭。

translations.literal: With the You clan his house had for generations been a powerful clan; the western prefectures had a saying: "Qu and You—livestock not worth counting by head."
translations.idiomatic: The Qu and You clans dominated the west for generations—folk rhymed: "Qu and You—too rich to count their oxen and sheep."

sentences.zh: 南開朱門，北望青樓。

translations.literal: Southward they open vermilion gates; northward they gaze on blue towers."
translations.idiomatic: Southward vermilion gates swing wide; northward green towers rise against the sky."

sentences.zh: 」洛陽傾覆，閻鼎等立秦王為皇太子于長安，鼎總攝百揆。
