translations.literal: " When Luoyang fell, Yan Ding and others established the Prince of Qin as imperial heir apparent at Chang'an; Ding oversaw all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell, Yan Ding and allies named the Prince of Qin heir apparent at Chang'an while Ding seized every portfolio.

sentences.zh: 允時為安夷護軍、始平太守，心害鼎功，且規權勢，因鼎殺京兆太守梁綜，乃與綜弟馮翊太守緯等攻鼎，走之。

translations.literal: Yun was then Protector of Anyi and Administrator of Shiping; he envied Ding's achievement and also coveted power—because Ding killed Administrator of Jingzhao Liang Zong, he joined Zong's younger brother Wei, Administrator of Fengyi, and others to attack Ding and drive him off.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun then guarded Anyi and governed Shiping; jealous of Ding's clout, he used Ding's murder of Liang Zong of Jingzhao as pretext to join Liang's brother Wei of Fengyi in driving Ding out.

sentences.zh: 會雍州刺史賈疋為屠各所殺，允代其任。

translations.literal: When Inspector of Yong Province Jia Ya was killed by the Tuge tribe, Yun succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuge tribesmen killed Inspector Jia Ya of Yong, Yun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 湣帝即尊位，以允為尚書左僕射、領軍、持節、西戎校尉、錄尚書事，雍州如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min took the throne, Yun was made Vice Director of the Left of the Secretariat, concurrent leader of the armies, credential bearer, Colonel of Western Tribes, recorder of Secretariat affairs, while Yong Province remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min named Yun Vice Director of the Left, chief of palace armies, credential bearer, Colonel of Western Rong, and overseer of the Secretariat while he kept Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 時劉曜、殷凱、趙染數萬眾逼長安，允擊破之，擒凱於陣。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Yao, Yin Kai, and Zhao Ran with tens of thousands pressed Chang'an; Yun defeated them and captured Kai in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao, Yin Kai, and Zhao Ran pressed Chang'an with tens of thousands—Yun routed them and seized Kai on the field.

sentences.zh: 曜復攻北地，允為太都督、驃騎將軍，次於青白城以救之。

translations.literal: Yao again attacked Beidi; Yun was Grand Commander and chief commander, halted at Qingbai City to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao struck Beidi again, Yun took supreme command as chief commander and camped at Qingbai City to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 曜聞而轉寇上郡，允軍于靈武，以兵弱不敢進。

translations.literal: Yao heard and turned to raid Shangjun; Yun stationed at Lingwu—troops weak and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yao veered to raid Shangjun; Yun halted at Lingwu but dared not advance—his force was too weak.

sentences.zh: 曜後復圍北地，太守麴昌遣使求救，允率步騎赴之。

translations.literal: Yao later again besieged Beidi; Administrator Qu Chang sent envoys begging rescue; Yun led infantry and cavalry to hurry there.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao besieged Beidi again, Administrator Qu Chang begged for aid—Yun marched infantry and cavalry to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 去城數十里，群賊繞城放火，煙塵蔽天，縱反間詐允曰：「郡城已陷，焚燒向盡，無及矣。

translations.literal: Several tens of li from the city, bandits ringed the city lighting fires—smoke and dust hid the sky—and spread false rumors to trick Yun: "The commandery city has fallen and is nearly burned out—too late."
translations.idiomatic: Tens of li short of the city, raiders ringed the walls with fire until smoke blotted the sky; agents lied to Yun that Beidi had fallen and every building burned—no point rushing on.

sentences.zh: 」允信之，眾懼而潰。

translations.literal: " Yun believed it; the host feared and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Yun believed them; his army panicked and melted away.

sentences.zh: 後數日，麴昌突圍赴長安，北地遂陷。

translations.literal: Several days later Qu Chang broke out and rushed to Chang'an; Beidi then fell.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Qu Chang broke out and raced to Chang'an—Beidi was lost.

sentences.zh: 允性仁厚，無威斷，吳皮、王隱之徒，無賴凶人，皆加重爵，新平太守竺恢，始平太守楊像、扶風太守竺爽、安定太守焦嵩，皆征鎮杖節，加侍中、常侍，村塢主帥小者，猶假銀青、將軍之號，欲以撫結眾心。

translations.literal: Yun was by nature humane and thick, without stern decisiveness; Wu Pi, Wang Yin, and such worthless villains all received high noble ranks; Administrators Zhu Hui of Xinping, Yang Xiang of Shiping, Zhu Shuang of Fufeng, Jiao Song of Anding—all held regional commands with staffs of authority, concurrent Palace Attendants and Permanent Attendants; even minor fort chiefs received silver-green ribbons and general's titles—intending thereby to soothe and bind popular hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was gentle and hesitant—worthless brutes like Wu Pi and Wang Yin won lofty titles; Zhu Hui, Yang Xiang, Zhu Shuang, and Jiao Song held frontier commands with staffs and court sinecures; even petty fortress chiefs wore silver-green ribbons and general's ribbons—all Yun's attempt to buy loyalty.

sentences.zh: 然諸將驕恣，恩不及下，人情頗離，由是羌胡因此跋扈，關中淆亂，劉曜復攻長安，百姓饑甚，死者太半。

translations.literal: Yet the generals grew arrogant and unrestrained; grace did not reach the lower ranks—popular feeling largely drifted away—thereupon Qiang and Hu took advantage to run riot; Guanzhong fell into chaos; Liu Yao again attacked Chang'an; the common people starved terribly—more than half died.
translations.idiomatic: Yet commanders grew arrogant and withheld favors from the ranks—popular sympathy frayed—so Qiang and Hu tribes rampaged and Guanzhong slid into chaos; Liu Yao struck Chang'an again while famine killed more than half the population.

sentences.zh: 久之，城中窘逼，帝將出降，歎曰：「誤我事者，麴、索二公也。

translations.literal: After a long time the city was sore pressed; the emperor was about to go out and surrender, sighing: "Those who misled my affairs are the two dukes Qu and Suo."
translations.idiomatic: Months of siege reduced the court—about to surrender in person, the emperor groaned: "Qu Yun and Suo Jing misled me."

sentences.zh: 」帝至平陽，為劉聰所幽辱，允伏地號哭不能起。

translations.literal: " When the emperor reached Pingyang he was humiliated in confinement by Liu Cong; Yun collapsed weeping on the ground and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingyang Liu Cong humiliated the captive sovereign—Qu Yun threw himself down and sobbed until he could not stand.

sentences.zh: 聰大怒，幽之於獄，允發憤自殺。

translations.literal: Cong was furious and imprisoned him in jail; Yun in rage killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Cong threw him in prison in fury—Qu Yun killed himself in despair.

sentences.zh: 聰嘉其忠烈，贈車騎將軍，諡節湣侯。

translations.literal: Cong praised his devoted martyrdom and posthumously awarded General of Chariots and Cavalry, posthumous title Marquis Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: Cong honored his loyalty with posthumous rank General of Chariots and Cavalry and the epithet Marquis Jiemin.

translations.literal: Diagram divider printed as an equals sign in the source.
translations.idiomatic: Printed edition inserts a sectional diagram marker here.

sentences.zh: 附 焦嵩

translations.literal: Appendix: Jiao Song
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Jiao Song

translations.literal: Second diagram divider equals sign in the printed edition.
translations.idiomatic: Another sectional illustration marker from the woodblock layout.

sentences.zh: 焦嵩，安定人。

translations.literal: Jiao Song was a man of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Song came from Anding.

sentences.zh: 初率眾據雍。

translations.literal: At first he led a host and held Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He first led troops holding Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 曜之逼京都，允告難於嵩，嵩素侮允，曰：「須允困，當救之。

translations.literal: When Yao threatened the capital, Yun reported distress to Song; Song had always despised Yun and said: "I must wait until Yun is desperate—then I will save him."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao threatened Chang'an, Qu Yun begged Jiao Song for help; Song, who had always scorned Yun, sneered: "I'll rescue him once he's desperate enough."

sentences.zh: 」及京都敗，嵩亦尋為寇所滅。

translations.literal: " When the capital fell, Song soon afterward was also destroyed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Song himself perished to raiders soon after.

sentences.zh: 賈渾

translations.literal: Jia Hun
translations.idiomatic: Jia Hun

sentences.zh: 賈渾，不知何郡人也。

translations.literal: Jia Hun—his native commandery is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Hun's birthplace went unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 太安中，為介休令。

translations.literal: In the Tai'an era he was magistrate of Jiexiu.
translations.idiomatic: During Tai'an he served as magistrate of Jiexiu.

sentences.zh: 及劉元海作亂，遣其將喬晞攻陷之。

translations.literal: When Liu Yuan rebelled, Yuan sent his general Qiao Xi to capture it.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuan rebelled, he sent Qiao Xi to storm the county.

sentences.zh: 渾抗節不降，曰：「吾為晉守，不能全之，豈苟求生以事賊虜，何面目以視息世間哉！

translations.literal: Hun held his integrity and would not surrender, saying: "I guard for Jin—unable to preserve it whole—how could I seek life by serving bandit invaders—what face would I have to draw breath in the world!"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Hun refused surrender: "I hold office for Jin—since I could not save the county, I will not cling to life under bandits—what face would I have among men!"

sentences.zh: 」晞怒，執將殺之，晞將尹崧曰：「將軍舍之，以勸事君。

translations.literal: " Xi was angry and seized him to kill him; Xi's officer Yin Song said: "General, spare him—to encourage service to lords.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Xi meant to execute him; officer Yin Song pleaded: "Spare him as an example of loyalty to one's lord."

sentences.zh: 」晞不聽，遂害之。

translations.literal: " Xi did not listen and therefore harmed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi refused and killed him.

sentences.zh: 王育

translations.literal: Wang Yu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu

sentences.zh: 王育，字伯春，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yu, courtesy name Bochun, was a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, courtesy name Bochun, hailed from Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，為人傭牧羊，每過小學，必歔欷流涕。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he hired out shepherding sheep for others; whenever he passed a village school he always sobbed and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and orphaned early, he hired out as a shepherd—passing village schools he always wept.

sentences.zh: 時有暇，即折蒲學書，忘而失羊，為羊主所責，育將鬻己以償之。

translations.literal: When he had spare time he broke rushes to practice writing—forgetting and losing sheep—blamed by the sheep owner; Yu was about to sell himself to compensate.
translations.idiomatic: He stole moments to scratch letters on rushes—lost sheep and faced his master's wrath—ready to sell himself to pay.

sentences.zh: 同郡許子章，敏達之士也，聞而嘉之，代育償羊，給其衣食，使與子同學，遂博通經史。

translations.literal: Xu Zizhang of the same commandery, a keen and accomplished man, heard and praised him; he compensated Yu's sheep for him and supplied clothes and food, had him study with his sons—thereupon Yu broadly mastered classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zizhang of the same commandery, a generous scholar, paid his debt, clothed and fed him, and enrolled him beside his sons until Yu mastered the canon.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺餘，須長三尺，容貌絕異，音聲動人。

translations.literal: His height exceeded eight chi; his beard was three chi; his appearance was strikingly unusual; his voice moved others.
translations.idiomatic: He stood over eight chi tall with a three-chi beard—features unforgettable, voice compelling.

sentences.zh: 子章以兄之子妻之，為立別宅，分之資業，育受之無愧色。

translations.literal: Zizhang married his elder brother's daughter to him, built him a separate residence, and divided property with him—Yu accepted without shame.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhang married a niece to him, built him a house, and split property—Yu accepted without false modesty.

sentences.zh: 然行己任性，頗不偶俗。

translations.literal: Yet in conduct he indulged his nature and largely did not conform to common ways.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he followed his own bent and ignored fashionable manners.

sentences.zh: 妻喪，吊之者不過四五人，然皆鄉閭名士。

translations.literal: At his wife's funeral only four or five mourners came—yet all were eminent men of village and lane.
translations.idiomatic: Only four or five mourners attended his wife's funeral—all were local worthies.

sentences.zh: 太守杜宣命為主簿。

translations.literal: Administrator Du Xuan appointed him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Du Xuan named him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 俄而宣左遷萬年令，杜令王攸詣宣，宣不迎之，攸怒曰：「卿往為二千石，吾所敬也。

translations.literal: Shortly Xuan was transferred down to magistrate of Wannian; Magistrate Wang You called on Xuan—Xuan did not go out to welcome him; You angrily said: "You formerly held two thousand shi—we respected you."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Du Xuan became magistrate of Wannian; Wang You of Duling visited—Xuan refused a reception—You snapped: "You once ranked two thousand shi—I honored you."

sentences.zh: 今吾儕耳，何故不見迎？

translations.literal: Now we are peers—why do you not come welcome me?
translations.idiomatic: We are equals now—why no welcome?

sentences.zh: 欲以小雀遇我，使我畏死鷂乎？

translations.literal: Do you mean to treat me like a little sparrow and make me fear a death hawk?
translations.idiomatic: Do you treat me like a sparrow and expect terror before your goshawk?

sentences.zh: 」育執刀叱攸曰：「君辱臣死，自昔而然。

translations.literal: " Wang Yu seized a knife and shouted at You: "When the lord is insulted the minister dies—it has been so since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu drew a blade and roared at Magistrate You: "When the master is shamed, his man must die—the rule is ancient."

sentences.zh: 我府君以非罪黜降，如日月之蝕耳，小縣令敢輕辱吾君！

translations.literal: Our prefect was dismissed without crime—like an eclipse of sun or moon—how dare a petty county magistrate lightly insult our lord!
translations.idiomatic: Our prefect fell without guilt—like a passing eclipse—how dare a county clerk insult him!

sentences.zh: 汝謂吾刀鈍邪，敢如是乎！

translations.literal: Do you say my blade is dull—how dare you behave thus!
translations.idiomatic: You think this blade dull—how dare you!

sentences.zh: 」前將殺之。

translations.literal: " He stepped forward to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed forward to strike.

sentences.zh: 宣懼，跣下抱育，乃止。

translations.literal: Xuan feared, slipped barefoot down and embraced Yu—only then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sprang barefoot to hug him still.

sentences.zh: 自此知名。

translations.literal: From this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: His name spread from that day.

sentences.zh: 司徒王渾辟為掾，除南武陽令。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Wang Hun summoned him as aide; he was appointed magistrate of Nanwuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Wang Hun took him as aide, then named him magistrate of Nanwuyang.

sentences.zh: 為政清約，宿盜逃奔他郡。

translations.literal: His governance was clear and restrained—long-standing bandits fled to other commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was spare and clean—veteran bandits fled to other counties.

sentences.zh: 遷并州督護。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervisor of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Bing Province supervisor.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎在鄴，又以育為振武將軍。

translations.literal: Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying was at Ye and again made Yu General Who Rouses Might.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying, camped at Ye, added the title General Who Rouses Might.

sentences.zh: 劉元海之為北單于，育說穎曰：「元海今去，育請為殿下促之，不然，懼不至也。

translations.literal: When Liu Yuan became Northern Chanyu, Yu urged Ying: "Yuan is departing now—I beg to hurry him for Your Highness—otherwise I fear he will not come."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuan became Northern Chanyu, Yu urged Ying: "Let me ride after him now or he may never come."

sentences.zh: 」穎然之，以育為破虜將軍。

translations.literal: " Ying agreed and made Yu General Who Breaks the Caitiffs.
translations.idiomatic: Ying agreed and named him General Who Breaks the Caitiffs.

sentences.zh: 元海遂拘之，其後以為太傅。

translations.literal: Yuan then detained him; afterward appointed him Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan seized him—later raised him to Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 韋忠

translations.literal: Wei Zhong
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhong

sentences.zh: 韋忠字子節，平陽人也。

translations.literal: Wei Zhong, courtesy name Zijie, was a man of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhong, courtesy name Zijie, came from Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 少慷慨，有不可奪之志。

translations.literal: From youth he was impassioned and had an unshakeable will.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he burned with principle nothing could break.

sentences.zh: 好學博通，性不虛諾。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was broadly conversant; by nature he did not make empty promises.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and kept every pledge.

sentences.zh: 閉門修己，不交當世，每至吉凶，親表贈遺，一無所受。

translations.literal: He closed his gate and cultivated himself, did not mingle with contemporaries; whenever kin came with gifts for auspicious or inauspicious occasions he accepted nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He shut his gate, shunned fashion, and refused every gift from kin at weddings or funerals.

sentences.zh: 年十二，喪父，哀慕毀悴，杖而後起。

translations.literal: At twelve he lost his father; he mourned in grief emaciation and needed a staff to rise.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he buried his father—grief wasted him until he needed a cane to rise.

sentences.zh: 司空裴秀吊之，匍匐號訴，哀慟感人。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Pei Xiu condoled with him; he crawled and wailed his grievance—his grief moved others.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Pei Xiu condoled—Zhong crawled forward wailing until listeners wept.

sentences.zh: 秀出而告人曰：「此子長大必為佳器。

translations.literal: Xiu went out and told people: "This boy when grown will surely become fine timber.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xiu left saying: "This boy will be worthy timber grown."

sentences.zh: 」歸而命子頠造焉。

translations.literal: " On returning he ordered his son Yi to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his son Pei Yi to call.

sentences.zh: 服闋，遂廬於墓所。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he therefore built a hut at the tomb site.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he built a hut at his father's tomb.

sentences.zh: 頠慕而造之，皆托行不見。

translations.literal: Yi admired him and went to visit—both times Zhong pleaded absence and did not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yi admired him and visited twice—Zhong pleaded errands and refused audience.

sentences.zh: 家貧，藜藿不充，人不堪其憂，而忠不改其樂。

translations.literal: His household was poor—wild greens scarcely enough—others could not endure such sorrow yet Zhong did not alter his joy.
translations.idiomatic: His house knew hunger—wild greens barely filled the bowl—others would despair; Zhong stayed content.

sentences.zh: 頠為僕射，數言之于司空張華，華辟之，辭疾不起。

translations.literal: When Yi became Vice Director, he repeatedly spoke of Zhong to Minister of Works Zhang Hua; Hua summoned him—Zhong declined illness and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Yi rose to Vice Director he praised Zhong to Zhang Hua—Zhang summoned him but Zhong pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，忠曰：「吾茨簷賤士，本無宦情。

translations.literal: People asked his reason; Zhong said: "I am a mean scholar under a thatched roof—originally without appetite for office.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said: "I am a nobody under a thatched eaves—no taste for office."

sentences.zh: 且茂先華而不實，裴頠欲而無厭，棄典禮而附賊後，若此，豈大丈夫之所宜行邪！

translations.literal: Moreover Maoxian is flowery without substance; Pei Yi desires without satiety—they abandon canonical rites and attach themselves to villain successors—with conduct like this, how could it be fitting for a great man!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Zhang Hua blooms without fruit; Pei Yi covets without limit—they betray ritual and cling to usurpers—what worthy man would walk that road!"

sentences.zh: 裴常有心托我，常恐洪濤蕩岳，餘波見漂，況可臨尾閭而窺沃焦哉！

translations.literal: Pei Yi has always wished to patronize me; I always feared great billows would scour the peaks and survivors drift on the wake—how much more dare I cling to Weilu's torrent and peek at Wojiao's shoals!
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yi keeps pressing his patronage—I dread tidal waves that bury mountains and folk tossed on the backwash; why would I cling to the cosmic drain or stare into the burning shoal?

sentences.zh: 」太守陳楚迫為功曹。

translations.literal: " Administrator Chen Chu compelled him to serve as merit evaluator.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Chen Chu forced him into the merit-evaluator post.

sentences.zh: 會山羌破郡，楚攜子出走，賊射之，中三創。

translations.literal: When Shanqiang tribes smashed the commandery, Chu fled carrying his son—the bandits shot them and struck three wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain Qiang raiders shattered the district; Chu fled with his son until bandits shot them three times.

sentences.zh: 忠冒刃伏楚。

translations.literal: Zhong braved blades to shield Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong threw himself onto Chu beneath the blades.

sentences.zh: 以身捍之，泣曰：「韋忠願以身代君，乞諸君哀之。

translations.literal: Using his body to defend him, weeping he said: "Wei Zhong wishes to substitute body for lord—I beg you gentlemen pity him."
translations.idiomatic: Covering Chu with his body he wept: "Take me instead—spare him."

sentences.zh: 」亦遭五矢。

translations.literal: " He also suffered five arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Five shafts struck him as well.

sentences.zh: 賊相謂曰：「義士也！

translations.literal: The bandits said to each other: "A man of principle!"
translations.idiomatic: The bandits murmured: "A true righteous man!"

sentences.zh: 」舍之。

translations.literal: " They released him.
translations.idiomatic: They let them go.

sentences.zh: 忠於是負楚以歸。

translations.literal: Zhong therefore carried Chu on his back home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong bore Chu home across his shoulders.

sentences.zh: 後仕劉聰，為鎮西大將軍，平羌校尉，討叛羌，矢盡，不屈節而死。

translations.literal: Later he served Liu Cong as Grand General Who Guards the West and Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang; campaigning against rebel Qiang he exhausted his arrows and died without yielding his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Cong he became Grand General Who Guards the West and Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang—fighting rebel Qiang until his arrows failed, he died unbroken.

sentences.zh: 辛勉

translations.literal: Xin Mian
translations.idiomatic: Xin Mian

sentences.zh: 辛勉，字伯力，隴西狄道人也。

translations.literal: Xin Mian, courtesy name Boli, was a man of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Mian, courtesy name Boli, came from Didao in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 父洪，左衛將軍。

translations.literal: His father Hong was General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin Hong had served as General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 勉博學，有貞固之操。

translations.literal: Mian was broadly learned and held steadfast integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and held unyielding principle.

sentences.zh: 懷帝世，累遷為侍中。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Huai he rose in stages to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huai he climbed to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽陷，隨帝至平陽。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell he followed the emperor to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell he followed the captive court to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 劉聰將署為光祿大夫，勉固辭不受。

translations.literal: Liu Cong wished to appoint him Household Grandee—Mian firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong offered him Household Grandee—Mian refused flatly.

sentences.zh: 聰遣其黃門侍郎喬度齎藥酒逼之，勉曰：「大丈夫豈以數年之命而虧高節，事二姓，下見武皇帝哉！

translations.literal: Cong sent his Palace Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Qiao Du with poisoned wine to force him; Mian said: "Would a great man trade a few years of life to dishonor lofty principle by serving two dynasties—and face Emperor Wu below!"
translations.idiomatic: Cong sent Qiao Du with poisoned wine; Mian replied: "No great man trades a handful of years for two masters—how could I face Emperor Wu below ground?"

sentences.zh: 」引藥將飲，度遽止之曰：「主上相試耳，君真高士也！

translations.literal: " He drew the medicine to drink—Du urgently stopped him saying: "The sovereign was only testing you—you are truly a lofty gentleman!"
translations.idiomatic: He lifted the cup—Du stopped him: "Only a test—you are every inch the noble recluse!"

sentences.zh: 」歎息而去。

translations.literal: " Du sighed and left.
translations.idiomatic: Du sighed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 聰嘉其貞節，深敬異之，為築室於平陽西山，月致酒米，勉亦辭而不受。

translations.literal: Cong praised his steadfast integrity and deeply revered him; he built him a chamber west of Pingyang mountain and monthly sent wine and rice—Mian again declined and accepted nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Cong honored his integrity, built him a lodge west of Pingyang, sent monthly rations—Mian refused every grain.

sentences.zh: 年八十，卒。

translations.literal: At eighty he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty.

translations.literal: Illustration equals-sign divider in the printed edition.
translations.idiomatic: Woodblock sectional marker between biographies.

sentences.zh: 勉族弟 賓

translations.literal: Mian's cousin Bin
translations.idiomatic: Xin Bin, cousin of Xin Mian

translations.literal: Second illustration divider printed as equals sign.
translations.idiomatic: Another plate marker from the engraved edition.

sentences.zh: 勉族弟賓，湣帝時為尚書郎。

translations.literal: Mian's cousin Bin—under Emperor Min he was Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Xin Bin served as Secretariat gentleman under Emperor Min.

sentences.zh: 及帝蒙塵于平陽，劉聰使帝行酒洗爵，欲觀晉臣在朝者意。

translations.literal: When the emperor suffered exile at Pingyang, Liu Cong made the emperor pour wine and wash cups—wishing to observe Jin ministers still at court.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingyang Liu Cong forced the Jin emperor to pour wine and rinse cups—probing which ministers still harbored loyalty.

sentences.zh: 賓起而抱帝大哭，聰曰：「前殺庾瑉輩，故不足為戒邪！

translations.literal: Bin rose and embraced the emperor, weeping loudly; Cong said: "Earlier we executed Yu Min and his sort—is this still no warning!"
translations.idiomatic: Bin sprang up to clutch the emperor and wail; Cong snarled: "Did executing Yu Min teach you nothing?"

sentences.zh: 」引出，遂加害焉。

translations.literal: " He led him out and then harmed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guards dragged Bin out and killed him.

sentences.zh: 劉敏元

translations.literal: Liu Minyuan
translations.idiomatic: Liu Minyuan

sentences.zh: 劉敏元，字道光，北海人也。

translations.literal: Liu Minyuan, courtesy name Daoguang, was a man of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Minyuan, courtesy name Daoguang, came from Beihai.

sentences.zh: 厲己修學，不以險難改心。

translations.literal: He disciplined himself in study and did not alter his heart because of peril.
translations.idiomatic: He honed himself through scholarship—hardship never bent his resolve.

sentences.zh: 好星曆陰陽術數，潛心《易》、《太玄》，不好讀史，常謂同志曰：「誦書當味義根，何為費功於浮辭之文！

translations.literal: He loved astrology, yin-yang, and numerology; he steeped himself in the Changes and Great Mystery—he did not love reading histories—often saying to like-minded men: "When chanting books one should savor the roots of meaning—why waste effort on florid rhetoric!"
translations.idiomatic: He studied astrology and the Changes, diving deep into the Great Mystery while spurning histories—telling friends: "Read for principle, not ornament."

sentences.zh: 《易》者，義之源，《太玄》，理之門，能明此者，即吾師也。

translations.literal: The Changes are the wellspring of meaning; the Great Mystery is the gate of principle—whoever clarifies these is my teacher.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes yield meaning; the Great Mystery opens principle—whoever masters them is my teacher."

sentences.zh: 」永嘉之亂，自齊西奔。

translations.literal: " In the Yongjia turmoil he fled west from Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongjia convulsed the realm he fled west from Qi.

sentences.zh: 同縣管平年七十餘，隨敏元而西，行及滎陽，為盜所劫。

translations.literal: Guan Ping of the same county, over seventy, followed Minyuan west; reaching Xingyang they were robbed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-year-old Guan Ping of his county followed him west until bandits ambushed them at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 敏元已免，乃還謂賊曰：「此公孤老，餘年無幾，敏元請以身代，願諸君舍之。

translations.literal: Minyuan had already escaped; he returned and said to the bandits: "This elder is orphaned and old—his remaining years are few—Minyuan begs to substitute body for him—I pray you gentlemen release him."
translations.idiomatic: Minyuan had broken free but walked back: "This old man is alone and nearly spent—take me instead and let him go."

sentences.zh: 」賊曰：「此公于君何親？

translations.literal: " The bandits said: "What kin is this elder to you?"
translations.idiomatic: The robbers asked: "What ties you to him?"

sentences.zh: 」敏元曰：「同邑人也。

translations.literal: " Minyuan said: "We are men of the same county."
translations.idiomatic: Minyuan said: "We share only a hometown."

sentences.zh: 窮窶無子，依敏元為命。

translations.literal: Impoverished and without sons, he relies on Minyuan for life.
translations.idiomatic: He is destitute and childless—his life hangs on mine.

sentences.zh: 諸君若欲役之，老不堪使，若欲食之，復不如敏元，乞諸君哀也。

translations.literal: If you gentlemen wish to labor him—old age cannot bear service; if you wish to eat him—again I am no match for Minyuan—I beg you gentlemen pity.
translations.idiomatic: Draft him and he cannot serve; eat him and I offer more meat—spare him out of pity."

sentences.zh: 」有一賊瞋目叱敏元曰：「吾不放此公，憂不得汝乎！

translations.literal: " One bandit glared and shouted at Minyuan: "If I do not release this elder, do you worry I cannot catch you!"
translations.idiomatic: A bandit glared: "Keep the old man—we still have you!"

sentences.zh: 」敏元奮劍曰：「吾豈望生邪！

translations.literal: " Minyuan brandished his sword and said: "Do I hope for life!"
translations.idiomatic: Minyuan whipped out steel: "I never counted on living!"

sentences.zh: 當殺汝而後死。

translations.literal: I shall kill you and then die.
translations.idiomatic: I'll kill you first—then die.

sentences.zh: 此公窮老，神祇尚當哀矜之。

translations.literal: This elder is poor and old—even spirits ought pity him.
translations.idiomatic: He is frail—even the gods should pity him.

sentences.zh: 吾親非骨肉，義非師友，但以見投之故，乞以身代。

translations.literal: We are not flesh-and-blood kin; righteousness is not teacher and friend—only because he entrusted himself to me I beg to substitute body.
translations.idiomatic: We are no kin by blood nor bond by teaching—he fled to me, so I offer my body instead.

sentences.zh: 諸大夫慈惠，皆有聽吾之色，汝何有靦面目而發斯言！

translations.literal: The gentlemen here are kind—all show faces inclined to hear me—how have you the brazen face to speak thus!
translations.idiomatic: Your chiefs lean toward mercy—how dare you alone shame them with threats!

sentences.zh: 」顧謂諸盜長曰：「夫仁義何常，寧可失諸君子！

translations.literal: " Turning to the bandit chiefs he said: "How can benevolence and duty ever be fixed—better lose them than betray gentlemen!"
translations.idiomatic: He turned to the bandit captains: "Honor demands consistency—would you lose it before gentlemen!"

sentences.zh: 上當為高皇、光武之事，下豈失為陳項乎！

translations.literal: Above one ought to do deeds like Emperor Gao and Guang Wu—below how could one fall short of Chen and Xiang!
translations.idiomatic: Reach upward like Gaozu or Guangwu—sink no lower than Chen She or Xiang Yu!"

sentences.zh: 當取之由道，使所過稱詠威德，柰何容畜此人以損盛美！

translations.literal: You ought to take power by the Way—make those you pass praise your awesome virtue—how can you harbor this man and harm supreme excellence!
translations.idiomatic: Win the realm by righteousness so travelers sing your virtue—why shelter such filth and spoil your name!

sentences.zh: 當為諸君除此人，以成諸君霸王之業。

translations.literal: I ought for you gentlemen remove this man—to complete your overlord enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Let me kill him for you—for the sake of your hegemony."

sentences.zh: 」前將斬之。

translations.literal: " He stepped forward to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: He lunged to strike the loudmouth down.

sentences.zh: 盜長遽止之，而相謂曰：「義士也！

translations.literal: The bandit chief urgently stopped him and they said to each other: "A man of principle!"
translations.idiomatic: The chief seized his arm: "A righteous man!"

sentences.zh: 害之犯義。

translations.literal: To harm him violates duty.
translations.idiomatic: To kill him violates honor.

sentences.zh: 」乃俱免之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they spared both.
translations.idiomatic: They freed both men.

sentences.zh: 後仕劉曜，為中書侍郎、太尉長史。

translations.literal: Later he served Liu Yao as Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat and senior clerk to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Yao he rose to Palace Secretariat gentleman and senior clerk to the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 周該

translations.literal: Zhou Gai
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Gai

sentences.zh: 周該，天門人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Gai was a man of Tianmen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Gai came from Tianmen.

sentences.zh: 性果烈，以義勇稱。

translations.literal: By nature he was resolute and fierce; he was famed for righteous courage.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and renowned for righteous daring.

sentences.zh: 雖不好學，而率由名教。

translations.literal: Though he did not love study, he followed the teaching of names and duties.
translations.idiomatic: He cared little for books yet lived by moral orthodoxy.

sentences.zh: 叔父級為宜都內史，亦忠節士也。

translations.literal: His uncle Ji was Interior Governor of Yidu—also a man of loyal integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Zhou Ji governed Yidu interior—another steadfast servant.

sentences.zh: 聞譙王承立義湘州，甘卓又不同王敦之舉，而書檄不至，級謂該曰：「吾嘗疾王敦挾陵上之心，今稱兵構逆，有危社稷之勢。

translations.literal: Hearing Prince of Qiao Cheng had raised loyal troops in Xiang Province and Gan Zhuo likewise opposed Wang Dun's movement—but letters and proclamations had not arrived—Ji said to Gai: "I have always resented Wang Dun's heart of lording over superiors; now he raises arms and frames rebellion—there is peril to the altars.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qiao Sima Cheng rallied Xiang Province and Gan Zhuo rejected Wang Dun—though word had not reached them—Zhou Ji told Gai: "Wang Dun always meant to bully the throne; now he rebels—the altars teeter."

sentences.zh: 譙王宗室之望，據方州之重，建旗誓眾，圖襲武昌。

translations.literal: Prince of Qiao is the imperial clan's hope—he holds regional weight—raises banners and swears the host—plans to strike Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng leads the royal house from Xiang Province—his banners rise for a blow at Wuchang."

sentences.zh: 甘安南少著勇名，士馬器械當今為盛，聞與譙王剋期舉義，此乃烈士急病之秋，吾致死之時也，汝其成吾之志，申款于譙王乎？

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the South Gan from youth has borne a brave name—troops, horses, and arms are now at their peak—I hear he has fixed a date with Prince of Qiao to raise righteous arms—this is the season when stalwarts rush to crisis—the time I give my death—will you fulfill my intent and declare sincerity to Prince of Qiao?"
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo of the south commands crack troops and agreed timing with Prince Cheng—this is the hour loyal men die—will you carry my pledge to the prince?"

sentences.zh: 」該欣然奉命，潛至湘州，與承相見，口陳至誠。

translations.literal: " Gai gladly accepted the charge; he secretly reached Xiang Province, met Cheng, and orally declared utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Gai slipped into Xiang Province and poured his heart out to Sima Cheng.

sentences.zh: 承大悅。

translations.literal: Cheng was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 會王敦遣其將魏乂圍承甚急，該乃與湘州從事周崎間出反命，俱為乂所見，考之至死，竟不言其故，級由是獲免王敦之難。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun sent his general Wei Yi to besiege Cheng urgently, Gai together with Xiang Province attendant Zhou Qi stole out to return report—both were spotted by Yi—tortured to death—they never spoke the reason—Ji thereby escaped Wang Dun's catastrophe.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Yi besieged Cheng, Gai and Zhou Qi slipped out with the reply—Yi caught them, tortured them to death, yet they revealed nothing—so Zhou Ji survived Wang Dun's purge.

sentences.zh: 桓雄

translations.literal: Huan Xiong
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xiong

sentences.zh: 桓雄，長沙人也。

translations.literal: Huan Xiong was a man of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xiong came from Changsha.

sentences.zh: 少仕州郡。

translations.literal: In youth he served in provincial posts.
translations.idiomatic: He began in minor provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 譙王承為湘州刺史，命為主簿。

translations.literal: Prince of Qiao Cheng was Inspector of Xiang Province and appointed him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng, as Inspector of Xiang Province, named him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 王敦之逆，承為敦將魏乂所執，佐吏奔散，雄與西曹韓階，從事武延並毀服為僮豎，隨承向武昌。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun rebelled, Cheng was seized by Dun's general Wei Yi; aides fled—Xiong together with Han Jie of the western bureau and attendant Wu Yan all tore their robes to pose as boys and followed Cheng toward Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Yi seized Cheng, staff fled—Huan Xiong, Han Jie, and Wu Yan disguised themselves as servants and followed Cheng toward Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 乂見雄姿貌長者，進退有禮，知非凡人，有畏憚之色，因害之。

translations.literal: Yi saw Xiong's imposing stature—advancing and retreating with ritual—knew he was no ordinary man—showed fear—and therefore killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi saw Xiong's bearing and manners—knew he was no servant—and slew him from fear.

sentences.zh: 韓階

translations.literal: Han Jie
translations.idiomatic: Han Jie

sentences.zh: 韓階，長沙人也。

translations.literal: Han Jie was a man of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jie came from Changsha.

sentences.zh: 性廉謹篤慎，為閭里所敬愛。

translations.literal: By nature he was honest, careful, and steadfast—respected and loved by village and lane.
translations.idiomatic: Honest and careful, he won local affection.

sentences.zh: 刺史、譙王承辟為議曹祭酒，轉西曹書佐。

translations.literal: Inspector Prince of Qiao Cheng summoned him as libationer of the deliberation bureau; he was transferred to clerk of the western bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng appointed him debate-master then western bureau clerk.

sentences.zh: 及承為魏乂所執，送武昌，階與武延等同心隨從，在承左右。

translations.literal: When Cheng was seized by Wei Yi and sent to Wuchang, Jie together with Wu Yan and others followed with one heart—stayed at Cheng's side.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi marched Cheng to Wuchang, Han Jie and Wu Yan stayed at his side.

sentences.zh: 桓雄被害之後，二人執志愈固。

translations.literal: After Huan Xiong was harmed, the two men's resolve grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Xiong died, they clung tighter to Cheng.

sentences.zh: 及承遇禍，階、延親營殯斂，送柩還都，朝夕哭奠，俱葬畢乃還。

translations.literal: When Cheng met disaster, Jie and Yan personally arranged burial and encoffining, sent the bier back to the capital, morning and evening wept offerings—not until both burials were complete did they return.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng fell, they laid him out, escorted the coffin home, mourned at dawn and dusk, and returned only after burial ended.

sentences.zh: 周崎

translations.literal: Zhou Qi
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qi

sentences.zh: 周崎，邵陵人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Qi was a man of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qi came from Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 為湘州從事。

translations.literal: He was attendant of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Xiang Province attendant.

sentences.zh: 王敦之難，譙王承使崎求救於外，與周該俱為魏乂偵人所執，乂責崎辭情，臨以白刃。

translations.literal: During Wang Dun's crisis Prince of Qiao Cheng sent Qi to beg rescue outside—together with Zhou Gai they were seized by Wei Yi's scouts—Yi pressed Qi's words and situation—threatened with bare blade.
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Dun's revolt Prince Cheng sent Zhou Qi for aid—scouts seized Qi and Zhou Gai—Yi interrogated Qi at swordpoint.

sentences.zh: 崎曰：「州將使求援於外，本無定指，隨時制宜耳。

translations.literal: Qi said: "The provincial commander sent me to seek rescue outside—originally there was no fixed plan—it adjusts to the moment."
translations.idiomatic: Qi said: "The governor sent me for help—no fixed plan—we adapt as needed."

sentences.zh: 」又謂崎曰：「汝為我語城中，稱大將軍已破劉隗、戴若思，甘卓住襄陽，無復異議，三江州郡，萬里肅清，外援理絕。

translations.literal: " He further said to Qi: "You shall tell the city for me—declare the Grand General has already defeated Liu Wei and Dai Ruosi; Gan Zhuo halts at Xiangyang—no further dissent—three-river provinces and commanderies, ten thousand li cleared—outside aid is logically cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Yi added: "Tell the city Wang Dun crushed Liu Wei and Dai Ruosi; Gan Zhuo sits idle at Xiangyang—the south is pacified—no hope of relief."

sentences.zh: 如是者，我當活汝。

translations.literal: If so, I shall spare you.
translations.idiomatic: Say that and you live."

sentences.zh: 」崎偽許之。

translations.literal: " Qi falsely promised him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi feigned agreement.

sentences.zh: 既到城下，大呼曰：「王敦軍敗于于湖，甘安南已克武昌，即日分遣大眾來赴此急，努力堅守，賊今散矣！

translations.literal: When he reached the foot of the walls he shouted loudly: "Wang Dun's army was defeated at Yuhu; General Who Pacifies the South Gan has already taken Wuchang—this very day he divides great hosts to hurry to this crisis—strive to hold fast—the bandits are scattered now!"
translations.idiomatic: At the walls he shouted: "Wang Dun lost at Yuhu Lake—Gan Zhuo took Wuchang—reinforcements march this way—hold fast—the rebels break!"

sentences.zh: 」乂於是數而殺之。

translations.literal: " Yi therefore enumerated his crimes and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had him executed for deceit.

sentences.zh: 易雄

translations.literal: Yi Xiong
translations.idiomatic: Yi Xiong

sentences.zh: 易雄，字興長，長沙瀏陽人也。

translations.literal: Yi Xiong, courtesy name Xingchang, was a man of Liuyang in Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Xiong, courtesy name Xingchang, came from Liuyang in Changsha.

sentences.zh: 少為縣吏，自念卑賤，無由自達，乃脫幘掛縣門而去。

translations.literal: In youth he was a county clerk; reflecting on his low mean status with no way to advance himself, he took off his headcloth, hung it on the county gate, and left.
translations.idiomatic: He clerked in the county—resenting low birth—he hung his turban on the yamen gate and walked away.

sentences.zh: 因習律令及施行故事，交結豪右，州里稍稱之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he studied statutes and ordinances and precedents of enactment, befriended powerful families—the province gradually praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered statutes and precedent, befriended local magnates, and earned a name.

sentences.zh: 仕郡，為主簿。

translations.literal: He served the commandery as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery took him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 張昌之亂也，執太守萬嗣，將斬之，雄與賊爭論曲直。

translations.literal: During Zhang Chang's rebellion they seized Administrator Wan Si and were about to behead him—Xiong debated right and wrong with the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chang seized Prefect Wan Si for execution, Yi Xiong argued justice with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，叱使牽雄斬之，雄趨出自若。

translations.literal: The bandits were angry and shouted to drag Xiong off to behead him—Xiong walked out calmly.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, they ordered him led to the block—he walked calmly to die.

sentences.zh: 賊又呼問之，雄對如初。

translations.literal: The bandits again called and questioned him—Xiong answered as at first.
translations.idiomatic: They questioned him again—he gave the same answer.

sentences.zh: 如此者三，賊乃舍之。

translations.literal: Three times thus—the bandits then released him.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he faced death unchanged—they released him.

sentences.zh: 嗣由是獲免，雄遂知名。

translations.literal: Si thereby escaped harm—Xiong then became known.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Si lived—and Yi Xiong's name spread.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，為州主簿，遷別駕。

translations.literal: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, he became provincial registrar and was promoted regional clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended Filial and Incorrupt, he rose from registrar to chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 自以門寒，不宜久處上綱，謝職還家。

translations.literal: Believing his lineage humble—unsuited to long holding upper offices—he resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking his family too lowly for high office, he resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 後為舂陵令。

translations.literal: Later he was magistrate of Chungling.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Chungling county.

sentences.zh: 刺史、譙王承既距王敦，將謀起兵以赴朝廷。

translations.literal: Inspector Prince of Qiao Cheng, having already resisted Wang Dun, planned to raise troops to hurry to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng, who already defied Wang Dun, meant to march to help the throne.

sentences.zh: 雄承符馳檄遠近，列敦罪惡，宣募縣境，數日之中，有眾千人，負糧荷戈而從之。

translations.literal: Xiong bore credentials and galloped proclamations far and near, listing Dun's crimes—issued summons across the county—within several days he had a thousand hosts bearing grain and shouldering halberds following him.
translations.idiomatic: He rode out edicts denouncing Dun's crimes and raised a thousand men with grain and spears within days.

sentences.zh: 承既固守，而湘中殘荒之後，城池不完，兵資又闕。

translations.literal: Cheng though defending steadfastly—after Xiang lay ruined—walls incomplete—arms and supplies lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng held out, but Xiang was wasted—walls broken, arms and grain short.

sentences.zh: 敦遣魏乂、李恆攻之，雄勉厲所統，捍禦累旬，士卒死傷者相枕。

translations.literal: Dun sent Wei Yi and Li Heng to attack—Xiong exhorted his command—defended successive tens of days—soldiers dead and wounded piled like pillows.
translations.idiomatic: Dun sent Wei Yi and Li Heng; Xiong rallied the defense for weeks while casualties piled up.

sentences.zh: 力屈城陷，為乂所虜，意氣慷慨，神無懼色。

translations.literal: Strength exhausted—the city fell—seized by Yi—bearing lofty spirit—his bearing fearless.
translations.idiomatic: When strength failed and the city fell to Yi, Xiong stood bold and unafraid.

sentences.zh: 送到武昌，敦遣人以檄示雄而數之。

translations.literal: Sent to Wuchang—Dun sent men to show Xiong the proclamation and rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuchang Dun had him shown the indictment and rebuked.

sentences.zh: 雄曰：「此實有之，惜雄位微力弱不能救國之難。

translations.literal: Xiong said: "Those deeds truly occurred—I regret rank slight and strength weak—unable to rescue the state's distress."
translations.idiomatic: Xiong admitted it all: "I was too small to save the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 王室如毀。

translations.literal: The royal house is like burning wreckage.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Jin is collapsing.

sentences.zh: 雄安用生為！

translations.literal: Of what use is Xiong's life!
translations.idiomatic: Why prolong my life?

sentences.zh: 今日即戮，得作忠鬼，乃所願也。

translations.literal: To die here today—becoming a loyal ghost—is my wish."
translations.idiomatic: Kill me now—I go gladly as a loyal ghost."

sentences.zh: 」敦憚其辭正，釋之。

translations.literal: Dun feared his upright words—released him.
translations.idiomatic: Dun respected his stance and let him go.

sentences.zh: 眾人皆賀，雄笑曰：「昨夜夢乘車，掛肉其傍。

translations.literal: All congratulated—Xiong smiled: "Last night I dreamed riding in a cart—with meat hung beside it."
translations.idiomatic: Well-wishers crowded round; Xiong smiled: "I dreamed I rode in a cart with meat hung beside it."

sentences.zh: 夫肉必有筋，筋者斤也，車傍有斤，吾其戮乎！

translations.literal: Meat surely has sinews—sinews sound like jin (axe-weight); beside cart there is jin—I suppose I shall be executed!
translations.idiomatic: Meat brings sinews ('jin'); beside 'cart' it hints at the axe—I'll face the blade!

sentences.zh: 」尋而敦遣殺之。

translations.literal: Soon Dun sent to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Dun soon sent killers.

sentences.zh: 當時見者，莫不傷惋。

translations.literal: Observers of the time—none failed to grieve.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard mourned him.

sentences.zh: 樂道融

translations.literal: Le Daorong
translations.idiomatic: Le Daorong

sentences.zh: 樂道融，丹陽人也。

translations.literal: Le Daorong was a man of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Le Daorong came from Danyang.

sentences.zh: 少有大志，好學不倦，與朋友信，每約己而務周給，有國士之風。

translations.literal: From youth he had great aims—loved learning tirelessly—with friends he kept faith—always disciplined himself while striving to help others thoroughly—he bore the air of a peerless knight.
translations.idiomatic: Ambitious, tireless in study, faithful to friends, generous and disciplined—he had the bearing of a champion.

sentences.zh: 為王敦參軍。

translations.literal: He was adjutant to Wang Dun.
translations.idiomatic: He served Wang Dun as adjutant.

sentences.zh: 敦將圖逆，謀害朝賢，以告甘卓。

translations.literal: Dun was about to plot rebellion—planned to murder court worthies—and reported this to Gan Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Dun plotted treason and meant to kill ministers, he told Gan Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 卓以為不可，遲留不赴。

translations.literal: Zhuo deemed it impossible—delayed and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo refused and stalled.

sentences.zh: 敦遣道融召之。

translations.literal: Dun sent Daorong to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Dun dispatched Daorong to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 道融雖為敦佐，忿其逆節，因說卓曰：「主上躬統萬機，非專任劉隗。

translations.literal: Though Daorong was Dun's aide, he resented Dun's treason—thereupon urged Zhuo: "The sovereign personally directs myriad affairs—not solely trusting Liu Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Daorong hated Dun's treason and told Zhuo: "The emperor rules in person—the court does not belong to Liu Wei alone."

sentences.zh: 今慮七國之禍，故割湘州以削諸侯，而王氏擅權日久，卒見分政，便謂被奪耳。

translations.literal: Now fearing the calamity of the seven states—therefore carved Xiang Province to pare the feudal lords—yet the Wang clan monopolized power long—suddenly seeing government divided—they suppose themselves robbed.
translations.idiomatic: The court split Xiang Province like Han paring feudal power; the Wangs had held sway so long they mistook reform for theft.

sentences.zh: 王敦背恩肆逆，舉兵伐主，國家待君至厚，今若同之，豈不負義！

translations.literal: Wang Dun betrays grace and runs riot—raises arms to strike the sovereign—the state has treated you generously—if you join him now—how is that not betraying duty!
translations.idiomatic: Dun leads revolt against the generous throne—will you join him and betray every bond?

sentences.zh: 生為逆臣，死為愚鬼，永成宗黨之恥邪！

translations.literal: Living a traitor—dying a foolish ghost—would you forever shame your clan!
translations.idiomatic: Live a rebel, die a fool—would you shame your kin forever?

sentences.zh: 君當偽許應命，而馳襲武昌，敦眾聞之，必不戰自散，大勳可就矣。

translations.literal: You should pretend consent—then gallop to strike Wuchang—Dun's host hearing it will surely scatter without battle—great merit may be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Feign agreement, then strike Wuchang—Dun's army will collapse without a fight.

sentences.zh: 」卓大然之，乃與巴東監軍柳純等露檄陳敦過逆，率所統致討，又遣齎表詣台。

translations.literal: Zhuo greatly agreed—thereupon with Ba East intendant Liu Chun and others issued open proclamation listing Dun's crimes—led what he commanded to campaign—and also sent memorial to the terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo agreed, joined Liu Chun of Ba East in denouncing Dun, marched his troops, and memorialized the court.

sentences.zh: 卓怍不果決，且年老多疑，遂待諸方同進，出軍稽遲。

translations.literal: Zhuo was ashamed to be indecisive—and old and suspicious—therefore waited for all quarters to advance together—his army marched sluggishly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo wavered, old and suspicious, waited for allies, and moved too slowly.

sentences.zh: 至豬口，敦聞卓已下兵，卓兄子仰時為敦參軍，使仰求和于卓，令其旋軍。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhukou—Dun heard Zhuo had sent troops—Zhuo's nephew Yang then served as Dun's adjutant—Dun had Yang seek peace with Zhuo—ordering him to wheel the army back.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhukou Dun learned Zhuo moved; Zhuo's nephew Yang served Dun and brokered a false truce to turn Zhuo back.

sentences.zh: 卓信之，將旋，主簿鄧騫與道融勸卓曰：「將軍起義兵而中廢，為敗軍之將，竊為將軍不取。

translations.literal: Zhuo believed—was about to wheel—chief clerk Deng Qian together with Daorong urged Zhuo: "You raised loyal troops only to halt midway—to be a defeated general—I privately deem this unworthy for you."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo believed him and turned back; Deng Qian and Daorong warned: "Stopping halfway makes you a beaten general."

sentences.zh: 今將軍之下，士卒各求其利，一旦而還，恐不可得也。

translations.literal: Now under your command soldiers each seek their profit—once you turn back—I fear you may not obtain what you seek.
translations.idiomatic: Your men fight for gain—retreat now and you may lose everything.

sentences.zh: 」卓不從。

translations.literal: Zhuo did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo ignored them.

sentences.zh: 道融晝夜涕泣諫卓，憂憤而死。

translations.literal: Daorong day and night wept remonstrating Zhuo—grieving and angry he died.
translations.idiomatic: Daorong wept and pleaded until grief killed him.

sentences.zh: 虞悝

translations.literal: Yu Kui
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kui

sentences.zh: 虞悝，長沙人也。

translations.literal: Yu Kui was a man of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kui came from Changsha.

sentences.zh: 弟望，字子都。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wang, courtesy name Zidu.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yu Wang, courtesy name Zidu.

sentences.zh: 並有士操，孝悌廉信，為鄉黨所稱，而俱好臧否，以人倫為己任。

translations.literal: Both had gentlemen's conduct—filial, brotherly, honest—praised by village and township—and both loved to praise or blame—took sorting human relations as their duty.
translations.idiomatic: Both men lived upright—filial and trustworthy—and judged character bluntly.

sentences.zh: 少仕州郡，兄弟更為治中、別駕。

translations.literal: In youth they served province and commandery—the brothers alternated as personnel clerk and regional clerk.
translations.idiomatic: They alternated as provincial personnel clerk and chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 元帝為丞相，招延四方之士，多辟府掾，時人謂之「百六掾」。

translations.literal: When Yuan Di was Chancellor he summoned talents from four quarters—many appointed aides—people of the time called them the 'hundred-six aides.'
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Di ruled as chancellor he recruited aides—the cohort called the hundred-six.

sentences.zh: 望亦被召，恥而不應。

translations.literal: Wang also received summons—ashamed—did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wang was summoned but refused out of pride.

sentences.zh: 譙王承臨州，知其名，檄悝為長史。

translations.literal: Prince of Qiao Cheng came to the province—knowing their names—summoned Kui as senior clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng knew their fame and summoned Yu Kui as senior clerk.

sentences.zh: 未到，遭母喪。

translations.literal: Before arriving—met mourning for mother.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took office his mother died.

sentences.zh: 會王敦作逆，承往吊悝，因留與語曰：「吾前被詔，遣鎮此州，正以王敦專擅，防其為禍。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun rebelled—Cheng went to condole with Kui—therefore stayed and spoke: "I previously received edict—to guard this province—precisely because Wang Dun monopolized power—guarding against disaster."
translations.idiomatic: During Dun's revolt Cheng visited Kui's mourning hall and said he came to Xiang to hedge against Dun.

sentences.zh: 今敦果為逆謀，吾受任一方，欲率所領馳赴朝廷，而眾少糧乏，且始到貴州，恩信未著。

translations.literal: Now Dun indeed plots rebellion—I receive charge of one quarter—wish to lead what I command to gallop to the court—yet hosts are few—grain lacking—and newly arrived in your province—grace and trust not yet established.
translations.idiomatic: Dun has rebelled—Cheng wished to march east but lacked troops, grain, and local trust.

sentences.zh: 卿兄弟南夏之翹俊，而智勇遠聞，古人墨絰即戎，況今鯨鯢塞路，王室危急，安得遂罔極之情，忘忠義之節乎！

translations.literal: You brothers are the southland's finest—and famed for wit and courage—the ancients wore ink mourning yet bore arms—how much more now while whales block the roads—the royal house urgent—how can you indulge utmost grief—forget loyalty and duty!
translations.idiomatic: You two are Xiang's finest—will you cling to mourning while the throne burns?

sentences.zh: 如今起事，將士器械可以濟不？

translations.literal: If we rise now—can officers and arms suffice?
translations.idiomatic: If we act now—can we equip an army?

sentences.zh: 」悝、望對曰：「王敦居分陝之任，一旦構逆，圖危社稷，此天地所不容，人神所忿疾。

translations.literal: " Kui and Wang replied: "Wang Dun holds elder-of-Shan duty—once frames rebellion—plots peril to the altars—this Heaven and earth cannot tolerate—men and spirits rage.
translations.idiomatic: They answered: "Dun betrayed his charge—Heaven rejects him.

sentences.zh: 大王不以猥劣，枉駕訪及，悝兄弟並受國恩，敢不自奮！

translations.literal: Great king—thinking us mean—condescends to visit—we brothers both received state grace—how dare we not strain ourselves!
translations.idiomatic: You honor us—we owe Jin everything—we will fight.

sentences.zh: 今天朝中興，人思晉德，大王以宗子之親，奉信順而誅有罪，孰不荷戈致命！

translations.literal: Now the court revives—everyone longs for Jin virtue—great king—by kinship of imperial clan—carrying trust and obedience—to punish the guilty—who will not shoulder halberds and give life!
translations.idiomatic: The realm aches for Jin—you lead kin with right—every soldier will follow.

sentences.zh: 但鄙州荒弊，糧器空竭，舟艦寡少，難以進討。

translations.literal: Yet our province lies ruined—grain and arms exhausted—boats few—hard to advance and punish.
translations.idiomatic: But Xiang lies ruined—ships and grain are scarce.

sentences.zh: 宜且收眾固守，傳檄四方，其勢必分，然後圖之，事可捷也。

translations.literal: Better gather masses—hold fast—spread proclamation to four quarters—their momentum must scatter—then plan attack—victory may be swift.
translations.idiomatic: Gather forces, defend, broadcast denunciations—split Dun—then strike.

sentences.zh: 」承以為然，乃命悝為長史，望為司馬，督護諸軍。

translations.literal: Cheng deemed it right—thereupon ordered Kui senior clerk—Wang marshal—overseeing all armies.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng agreed—named Yu Kui senior clerk and Yu Wang marshal.

sentences.zh: 湘東太守鄭澹，敦之姊夫也，不順承旨，遣望討之。

translations.literal: Administrator of Xiangdong Zheng Dan—Dun's brother-in-law—did not obey Cheng's command—Cheng sent Wang to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zheng Dan of Xiangdong—Dun's brother-in-law—defied Cheng; Cheng sent Yu Wang against him.

sentences.zh: 望率眾一旅，直入郡斬澹，以徇四境。

translations.literal: Wang led one brigade—entered straight into the commandery—beheaded Dan—displayed through four borders.
translations.idiomatic: Wang took one column, stormed the prefecture, executed Dan, and posted the deed.

sentences.zh: 及魏乂來攻，望每先登，力戰而死。

translations.literal: When Wei Yi came attacking—Wang always scaled first—fought fiercely and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Yi attacked, Wang scaled walls first and fell fighting.

sentences.zh: 城破，悝復為乂所執，將害之，子弟對之號泣，悝謂曰：「人生有死，闔門為忠義鬼，亦何恨哉！

translations.literal: City broken—Kui again seized by Yi—about to harm him—sons and nephews weeping toward him—Kui told them: "Human life has death—whole household becoming ghosts of loyalty and duty—what regret!"
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Yi seized Yu Kui; as kin wept he said death together as loyal ghosts brings no shame.

sentences.zh: 」及王敦平，贈悝襄陽太守，望滎陽太守，遣謁者至墓，祭以少牢。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun was pacified—they posthumously awarded Kui Administrator of Xiangyang—Wang Administrator of Xingyang—sent herald to tombs—sacrificed with shao lao.
translations.idiomatic: After Dun fell they honored Yu Kui and Yu Wang posthumously and sacrificed at their graves.

sentences.zh: 沈勁

translations.literal: Shen Jin
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jin

sentences.zh: 沈勁，字世堅，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Jin, courtesy name Shijian, was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jin, courtesy name Shijian, came from Wukang.

sentences.zh: 父充，與王敦構逆，眾敗而逃，為部曲將吳儒所殺。

translations.literal: His father Chong collaborated with Wang Dun in rebellion—hosts defeated—fled—and was killed by household troop commander Wu Ru.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen Chong joined Wang Dun's rebellion, fled defeat, and died at Wu Ru's hands.

sentences.zh: 勁當坐誅，鄉人錢舉匿之得免。

translations.literal: Jin should have faced execution—townsman Qian Ju hid him—obtained exemption.
translations.idiomatic: He should have died for kin guilt—neighbor Qian Ju hid him.

sentences.zh: 其後竟殺仇人。

translations.literal: Afterward he killed his enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He later avenged his father.

sentences.zh: 勁少有節操，哀父死于非義，志欲立勳以雪先恥。

translations.literal: Jin from youth had integrity—grieved father died unjust—resolved to win merit to wipe ancestral shame.
translations.idiomatic: He burned to redeem his father's shame with deeds.

sentences.zh: 年三十餘，以刑家不得仕進。

translations.literal: Past thirty—because convict kin could not advance in office.
translations.idiomatic: His criminal lineage barred office past thirty.

sentences.zh: 郡將王胡之深異之，及遷平北將軍、司馬刺史，將鎮洛陽，上疏曰：「臣當籓衛山陵，式遏戎狄，雖義督群心，人思自百，然方翦荊棘，奉宣國恩，艱難急病，非才不濟。

translations.literal: Regional commander Wang Huzhi deeply esteemed him—when promoted Grand General Who Pacifies North and Inspector of Sima—about to garrison Luoyang—memorialized: "Your subject shall guard the imperial tombs—stem Rong and Di—though righteous discipline binds every heart—men wish to redouble effort—yet clearing brambles—spreading state grace—hardship and crisis—without talent it cannot be aided."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huzhi admired him; marching to Luoyang he memorialized for aid guarding the tombs.

sentences.zh: 吳興男子沈勁，清操著於鄉邦，貞固足以幹事。

translations.literal: Wuxing commoner Shen Jin—pure conduct famed in home district—steadfast integrity enough to manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Shen Jin's purity and competence.

sentences.zh: 且臣今西，文武義故，吳興人最多，若令勁參臣府事者，見人既悅，義附亦眾。

translations.literal: Moreover your subject going west—civil and martial old ties—Wuxing men most numerous—if you order Jin to join your headquarters—seen by men they rejoice—righteous attachment also abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Many Wuxing men followed him—appoint Jin and they rally.

sentences.zh: 勁父充昔雖得罪先朝，然其門戶累蒙曠蕩，不審可得特垂沛然，許臣所上否？

translations.literal: Though Jin's father Chong formerly offended prior court—yet his household repeatedly received sweeping grace—may it be specially granted—your subject's petition permitted?
translations.idiomatic: He asked clemency for Shen Chong's son.

sentences.zh: 」詔聽之。

translations.literal: Edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 勁既應命，胡之以疾病解職。

translations.literal: Jin having answered the summons—Huzhi because of illness resigned office.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jin joined him—then Huzhi quit from illness.

sentences.zh: 升平中，慕容恪侵逼山陵。

translations.literal: During the Shengping era—Murong Ke pressed the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengping Murong Ke threatened the Luoyang tombs.

sentences.zh: 時冠軍將軍陳祐守洛陽，眾不過二千，勁自表求配祐效力，因以勁補冠軍長史，令自募壯士，得千餘人，以助祐擊賊，頻以寡制眾。

translations.literal: At the time General Who Wins the Crown Chen You guarded Luoyang—hosts not exceeding two thousand—Jin personally memorialized asking to serve under You—thereupon supplemented Jin as senior clerk to General Who Wins the Crown—ordered him to recruit stalwart men—obtained over a thousand—to aid You striking bandits—repeatedly used few to control many.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang held two thousand men under Chen You; Shen Jin volunteered, recruited a thousand, and repeatedly beat larger forces.

sentences.zh: 而糧盡援絕，祐懼不能保全。

translations.literal: Yet grain exhausted—relief cut off—You feared unable to preserve intact.
translations.idiomatic: Food ran out and relief died—You despaired of holding the city.

sentences.zh: 會賊寇許昌，祐因以救許昌為名，興寧三年，留勁以五百人守城，祐率眾而東。

translations.literal: When bandits raided Xuchang—You therefore under pretext of relieving Xuchang—in Xingning third year—left Jin with five hundred men guarding the city—You led host east.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders threatened Xuchang, You used rescue as excuse—left Jin five hundred men in Xingning 3—and marched east.

sentences.zh: 會許昌已沒，祐因奔崖塢。

translations.literal: When Xuchang had already fallen—You therefore fled to Ya fort.
translations.idiomatic: Xuchang fell—You fled to the Ya redoubt.

sentences.zh: 勁志欲致命，欣獲死所。

translations.literal: Jin's resolve wished to give life—rejoiced to obtain place of death.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jin welcomed a place to die.

sentences.zh: 尋為恪所攻，城陷，被執，神氣自若。

translations.literal: Soon attacked by Ke—city fell—seized—spirit and bearing calm.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke took the city and captured him—calm to the end.

sentences.zh: 恪奇而將宥之，其中軍將軍慕容虔曰：「勁雖奇士，觀其志度，終不為人用。

translations.literal: Ke marveled and wished to spare him—his Central Army general Murong Qian said: "Though Jin is a strange man—observe his resolve—in the end he will not serve others—if you pardon—surely later trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Ke meant to spare him; Murong Qian warned he would never serve Yan.

sentences.zh: 今若赦之，必為後患。

translations.literal: If you spare—surely later disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Forgive him and he becomes your foe.

sentences.zh: 」遂遇害。

translations.literal: Thereupon harmed.
translations.idiomatic: They executed him.

sentences.zh: 恪還，從容言于慕容晞曰：「前平廣固，不能濟辟閭，今定洛陽而殺沈勁，實有愧于四海。

translations.literal: Ke returning—calmly said to Murong Xi: "Earlier pacifying Guanggu—could not preserve Pilü—now settling Luoyang yet killing Shen Jin—truly I have shame before four seas."
translations.idiomatic: Ke later admitted shame at killing Shen Jin after taking Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷聞而嘉之，贈東陽太守。

translations.literal: Court heard and praised—posthumously awarded Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court honored him posthumously as Dongyang prefect.

sentences.zh: 子赤黔為大長秋。

translations.literal: Son Chi Qian became Grand Chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen Chi Qian rose to Grand Chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 赤黔子叔任，義熙中為益州刺史。

translations.literal: Chi Qian's son Shuren—during Yixi became Inspector of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Qian's grandson Shuren governed Yi Province under Yixi.

sentences.zh: 吉挹

translations.literal: Ji Yi
translations.idiomatic: Ji Yi

sentences.zh: 吉挹，字祖沖，馮翊蓮芍人也。

translations.literal: Ji Yi, courtesy name Zuchong, was a man of Lianshao in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Yi, courtesy name Zuchong, came from Lianshao.

sentences.zh: 祖朗，湣帝時為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Grandfather Lang—under Emperor Min was Palace Assistant Clerk of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ji Lang served as censorate assistant under Emperor Min.

sentences.zh: 西朝不守，朗歎曰：「吾智不能謀，勇不能死，何忍君臣相隨北面事賊虜乎！

translations.literal: When western court could not be held—Lang sighed: "My wisdom cannot plan—courage cannot die—how endure ruler and minister together serving northern bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: When Chang'an fell Ji Lang said he could neither save nor die with honor—refused to bow north.

sentences.zh: 」乃自殺。

translations.literal: Thereupon killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He killed himself.

sentences.zh: 挹少有志節。

translations.literal: Yi from youth had resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Yi showed principle young.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝初，苻堅陷梁益，桓豁表挹為魏興太守，尋加輕車將軍，領晉昌太守。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign—Fu Jian captured Liang and Yi—Huan Huo memorialized Yi as Administrator of Weixing—soon added General of Agile Cavalry—concurrent Administrator of Jinchang.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian took Liangzhou and Yizhou, Huan Huo named him Weixing prefect and later Jinchang.

sentences.zh: 以距堅之功，拜員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: For merit resisting Jian—appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Beyond the Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He earned Cavalier Attendant for resisting Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 苻堅將韋鐘攻魏興，挹遣眾距之，斬七百餘級，加督五郡軍事。

translations.literal: Fu Jian's general Wei Zhong attacked Weixing—Yi sent hosts resisting—beheaded over seven hundred—added oversight of five commanderies' military.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhong struck Weixing—Ji Yi killed seven hundred and oversaw five commanderies.

sentences.zh: 鐘率眾欲趣襄陽，挹又邀擊，斬五千餘級。

translations.literal: Zhong led host wishing to hurry to Xiangyang—Yi again intercepted—beheaded over five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong turned toward Xiangyang—Yi ambushed and slew five thousand.

sentences.zh: 鐘怒，回軍圍之，挹又屢挫其銳。

translations.literal: Zhong angry—wheeled army besieging—Yi again repeatedly blunted their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong besieged the city—Yi broke his assaults again and again.

sentences.zh: 其後賊眾繼至，挹力不能抗，城將陷，引刃欲自殺，其友止之曰：「且苟存以展他計，為計不立，死未晚也。

translations.literal: Afterward enemy hosts arrived in succession—Yi's strength could not resist—city about to fall—drew blade wishing suicide—his friend stopped him saying: "Yet endure to devise other plans—if plans fail—death not yet late."
translations.idiomatic: When foes massed and the wall cracked, he drew steel to die—friends begged him to wait for another stratagem.

sentences.zh: 」挹不從，友人逼奪其刀。

translations.literal: Yi would not consent—a friend forced him and wrested away his blade.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Yi refused—his friend wrestled the knife from him.

sentences.zh: 會賊執之，挹閉口不言，不食而死。

translations.literal: When bandits seized him, Yi kept silent and would not eat until he died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took him; he sealed his lips and starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍桓沖上言曰：「故輕車將軍、魏興太守吉挹祖朗，西台傾覆，隕身守節。

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Huan Chong submitted: "The late General of Light Chariots and Administrator of Weixing Ji Yi, courtesy name Zulang—when the Western court collapsed—perished while holding his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong memorialized: "Ji Yi of Weixing died loyal when the western throne fell."

sentences.zh: 挹世篤忠孝，乃心本朝。

translations.literal: Yi through generations was steeped in loyalty and filial piety—his heart was fixed on this court.
translations.idiomatic: Generations of his house lived loyalty and filial piety; his heart stayed with Jin.

sentences.zh: 臣亡兄溫昔伐咸陽，軍次灞水，挹攜將二弟，單馬來奔，錄其此誠，仍加擢授，自新野太守轉在魏興。

translations.literal: Your subject's deceased elder brother Huan Wen once campaigned against Xianyang—the army halted at Ba River—Yi led two younger brothers and came alone on horseback to surrender us—recording that sincerity he was promoted—from Administrator of Xinye transferred to Weixing.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen marched on Xianyang, Ji Yi rode in with two brothers to serve Jin—so Wen moved him from Xinye to Weixing.

sentences.zh: 久處兵任，委以邊戍，疆場歸懷，著稱所蒞。

translations.literal: Long entrusted with military duty—assigned frontier defense—the borderlands submitted and praised him wherever he served.
translations.idiomatic: He held border commands so long the frontier rallied and spoke well of his tenure.

sentences.zh: 前年狡氏縱逸，浮河而下，挹孤城獨立，眾無一旅，外摧凶銳，內固津要，虜賊舟船，俘馘千計，而賊並力功圍，經歷時月，會襄陽失守，邊情沮喪，加眾寡勢殊，以至陷設。

translations.literal: The year before last hostile tribes broke loose—floated down the Yellow River—Yi stood alone in an isolated city—with not even a full brigade—without blunted the foe within he secured the ferries—seized enemy boats—captives and heads counted by thousands—yet the foe combined strength to besiege—for months—when Xiangyang fell frontier spirits sank—and odds were hopeless—until he was overrun and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes swept downriver while Yi held one town without reserves—harried boats and counted hundreds of kills—yet sieges dragged on until Xiangyang fell and he was lost.

sentences.zh: 挹辭氣慷慨，志在不辱，杖刃推戈，期之以隕，將吏持守，用不即斃，遂乃杜口無言，絕粒而死。

translations.literal: Yi spoke with generous valor—intent on avoiding dishonor—grasping spear and blade—expecting to fall—officers and clerks restrained him so he could not die at once—thereupon he sealed his lips—refused grain—and died.
translations.idiomatic: He defied capture with weapon in hand; men wrestled him back from suicide—so he shut his mouth and starved.

sentences.zh: 挹參軍史穎，近於賊中得還，齎挹臨終手疏，並具說意狀。

translations.literal: Yi's adjutant Shi Ying lately escaped from the enemy—bearing Yi's final handwritten memorial—and explained the full circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Shi Ying escaped with Ji Yi's deathbed note and the whole story.

sentences.zh: 挹之忠志，猶在可錄。

translations.literal: Yi's loyal resolve still merits recording.
translations.idiomatic: His loyalty still deserves the record.

sentences.zh: 若蒙天地垂曲宥之恩，則榮加枯朽，惠隆泉壤矣。

translations.literal: If Heaven and Earth might bend with forgiving grace—then glory would reach his dry bones and kindness wash the underworld.
translations.idiomatic: Grant tolerance and honor reaches even his bones below.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉之，追贈益州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this—posthumously awarded him Inspector of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved and named him Inspector of Yi posthumously.

sentences.zh: 王諒

translations.literal: Wang Liang
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang

sentences.zh: 王諒，字幼成，丹陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Liang, courtesy name Youcheng, was a man of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang, style Youcheng, came from Danyang.

sentences.zh: 少有幹略，為王敦所擢，參其府事，稍遷武昌太守。

translations.literal: In youth he had capacity and strategy—Wang Dun promoted him for headquarters duty—gradually promoted to Administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Dun spotted his talent—used him in staff work—and raised him to Wuchang prefect.

sentences.zh: 初，新昌太守梁碩專威交土，迎立陶咸為刺史。

translations.literal: At first Xinchang prefect Liang Shuo monopolized power in Jiao—welcomed Tao Xian as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shuo of Xinchang ruled Jiao like a tyrant and installed Tao Xian.

sentences.zh: 咸卒，王敦以王機為刺史，碩發兵距機，自領交趾太守，乃迎前刺史修則子湛行州事。

translations.literal: When Xian died—Wang Dun named Wang Ji inspector—Shuo raised troops to block Ji—appointed himself Jiaozhi prefect—then welcomed former inspector Xiu Ze's son Zhan to manage provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Tao Xian died, Dun sent Wang Ji; Shuo fought Ji, seized Jiaozhi, and put Xiu Zhan in charge.

sentences.zh: 永興三年，敦以諒為交州刺史。

translations.literal: In Yongxing third year Dun appointed Liang Inspector of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing 3: Dun made Wang Liang inspector of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 諒將之任，敦謂曰：「修湛、梁碩皆國賊也，卿至，便收斬之。

translations.literal: As Liang took up the post Dun told him: "Xiu Zhan and Liang Shuo are traitors to the state—when you arrive seize and execute them."
translations.idiomatic: Dun ordered him to arrest and kill Zhan and Shuo on arrival.

sentences.zh: 」諒既到境，湛退還九真。

translations.literal: When Liang reached the border—Zhan withdrew to Jiuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Liang crossed the frontier; Zhan fell back to Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史陶侃遣人誘湛來詣諒所，諒敕從人不得入閣，既前，執之。

translations.literal: Guangzhou Inspector Tao Kan sent men to lure Zhan to Liang's place—Liang ordered followers not to enter the inner chamber—when Zhan came forward Liang seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Kan baited Zhan to Liang—who barred escorts and seized Zhan inside.

sentences.zh: 碩時在坐，曰：「湛故州將之子，有罪可遣，不足殺也。

translations.literal: Shuo was present and said: "Zhan is a former inspector's son—if guilty banish him—no need to kill."
translations.idiomatic: Shuo pleaded: "He is an old colleague's son—exile him if you must."

sentences.zh: 」諒曰：「是君義故，無豫我事。

translations.literal: Liang said: "That is your bond of righteousness—none of my affair."
translations.idiomatic: Liang replied: "Your friendship—not my brief."

sentences.zh: 」即斬之。

translations.literal: He executed him at once.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded Zhan on the spot.

sentences.zh: 碩怒而出。

translations.literal: Shuo left in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo stormed out.

sentences.zh: 諒陰謀誅碩，使客刺之，弗克，遂率眾圍諒于龍編。

translations.literal: Liang secretly plotted to kill Shuo—sent retainers to stab him—they failed—Shuo then led troops besieging Liang at Longbian.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's assassins missed Shuo, who then besieged him at Longbian.

sentences.zh: 陶侃遣軍救之，未至而諒敗。

translations.literal: Tao Kan sent troops to rescue—before they arrived Liang was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Kan's relief column arrived too late.

sentences.zh: 碩逼諒奪其節，諒固執不與，遂斷諒右臂。

translations.literal: Shuo forced Liang to yield his tally—Liang refused firmly—Shuo severed Liang's right arm.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo demanded the credentials; Liang would not give—Shuo hacked off his right arm.

sentences.zh: 諒正色曰：「死且不畏，臂斷何有！

translations.literal: Liang said sternly: "I fear not death—what is a lost arm!"
translations.idiomatic: "Death does not frighten me—why fear losing an arm!"

sentences.zh: 」十餘日，憤恚而卒。

translations.literal: After ten-some days he died of rage.
translations.idiomatic: He died of wrath within a fortnight.

sentences.zh: 碩據交州，凶暴酷虐，一境患之，竟為侃軍所滅，傳首京都。

translations.literal: Shuo held Jiao Province—savage and cruel—the whole region suffered—Kan's army eventually destroyed him—his head sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo tyrannized Jiao until Kan wiped him out and sent his head north.

sentences.zh: 宋矩

translations.literal: Song Ju
translations.idiomatic: Song Ju

sentences.zh: 宋矩，字處規，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Song Ju, courtesy name Chugui, was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ju, style Chugui, came from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 慷慨有志節。

translations.literal: Generous in spirit—he had resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Spirited and principled.

sentences.zh: 張重華據涼州地，以矩為宛戍都尉。

translations.literal: Zhang Chonghua held Liangzhou—appointed Ju Warden of Yuan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua made him captain of the Yuan outpost.

sentences.zh: 石季龍遣將麻秋攻大夏，護軍梁式執太守宋晏，以城應秋。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong sent general Ma Qiu against Daxia—Protector Liang Shi seized prefect Song Yan and surrendered the city to Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu struck Daxia; Liang Shi handed prefect Song Yan and the walls to him.

sentences.zh: 秋遣晏以書致矩。

translations.literal: Qiu sent Yan with a letter summoning Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu used Yan's letter to lure Song Ju.

sentences.zh: 矩既至，謂秋曰：「辭父事君，當立功與義；

translations.literal: When Ju arrived he told Qiu: "Leaving father to serve ruler—one must achieve merit in righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Ju told Ma Qiu: "Serving the throne means earning merit through duty.

sentences.zh: 苟功義不立，當守名節。

translations.literal: If merit and righteousness are not established—one must guard name and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot—then guard your honor.

sentences.zh: 矩終不背主覆宗，偷生於世。

translations.literal: Ju would never betray his lord and ruin his clan—stealing life in this world.
translations.idiomatic: I will not betray my lord and disgrace my kin to cling to life."

sentences.zh: 」先殺妻子，自刎而死。

translations.literal: He first killed wife and children—then cut his throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: He slew his family then opened his own throat.

sentences.zh: 秋曰：「義士也！

translations.literal: Qiu said: "A man of righteousness!"
translations.idiomatic: "A true man!" cried Qiu.

sentences.zh: 」命葬之。

translations.literal: He ordered him buried with rites.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu had him buried honorably.

sentences.zh: 重華嘉其誠節，贈振威將軍。

translations.literal: Chonghua praised his fidelity—posthumously awarded General Who Shakes Might.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua honored him as General Who Shakes Might.

sentences.zh: 車濟

translations.literal: Che Ji
translations.idiomatic: Che Ji

sentences.zh: 車濟，字萬度，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Che Ji, courtesy name Wandu, was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Che Ji, style Wandu, came from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 果毅有大量。

translations.literal: Resolute and daring—he had great capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and magnanimous.

sentences.zh: 張重華以為金城令，為石季龍將麻秋所陷，濟不為秋屈。

translations.literal: Zhang Chonghua appointed him magistrate of Jincheng—taken by Shi Jilong's general Ma Qiu—Ji would not yield to Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu seized Jincheng; Che Ji refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 秋必欲降之，乃臨之以兵。

translations.literal: Qiu was determined to break him—therefore confronted him with armed troops.
