translations.idiomatic: Qiu ringed him with blades to force surrender.

sentences.zh: 濟辭色不撓，曰：「吾雖才非龐德，而受任同之。

translations.literal: Ji answered without flinching: "Though my talent does not match Pang De's—I bear the same charge.
translations.idiomatic: Ji said: "I am no Pang De—but I accepted the same duty.

sentences.zh: 身可殺，志不可移。

translations.literal: The body may be killed—the resolve cannot be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Kill this body—you cannot move my will."

sentences.zh: 」乃伏劍而死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he fell on his sword and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fell on his sword.

sentences.zh: 秋歎其忠節，以禮葬之。

translations.literal: Qiu admired his loyal integrity—buried him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu admired him and gave him a proper grave.

sentences.zh: 後重華迎致其喪，親臨慟哭，贈宜禾都尉。

translations.literal: Later Chonghua brought back his remains—went in person to mourn—posthumously awarded Commandant of Yihe.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua fetched his body home, wept over it, and named him Yihe commandant.

sentences.zh: 丁穆

translations.literal: Ding Mu
translations.idiomatic: Ding Mu

sentences.zh: 丁穆，字彥遠，譙國人也。

translations.literal: Ding Mu, courtesy name Yanyuan, was a man of Qiao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Mu, style Yanyuan, came from Qiao.

sentences.zh: 積功勞，封真定侯，累遷為順陽太守。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit enfeoffed Marquis of Zhending—promoted by stages to Administrator of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Merit made him Marquis of Zhending and eventually Shunyang prefect.

sentences.zh: ，除振武將軍、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Shakes Might and Inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Next he received General Who Shakes Might and Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 受詔未發，會苻堅遣眾寇順陽，穆戰敗，被執至長安，稱疾不仕偽朝。

translations.literal: Before he could depart on the edict—Fu Jian sent forces raiding Shunyang—Mu was defeated—captured to Chang'an—claimed illness and would not serve the usurping court.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up his post, Fu Jian smashed Shunyang; Mu fell captive to Chang'an and feigned sickness to shun Former Qin.

sentences.zh: 堅又傾國南寇，穆與關中人士唱義，謀襲長安，事泄，遇害，臨死作表以付其妻周。

translations.literal: When Jian again marched the whole realm south—Mu with Guanzhong worthies raised righteousness—plotted to strike Chang'an—the plot leaked—he was killed—facing death he drafted a memorial for his wife Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian invaded south, Mu plotted a Chang'an coup with Guanzhong men—it failed; he drafted a last memorial for Lady Zhou.

sentences.zh: 其後周得至京師，詣闕上之。

translations.literal: Later Zhou reached the capital—presented it at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhou brought it to the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝下詔曰：「故順陽太守、真定侯丁穆力屈身陷，而誠節彌固，直亮壯勁，義貫古烈。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu's edict: "Former Administrator of Shunyang—Marquis of Zhending Ding Mu—strength spent yet trapped—yet loyal integrity grew firmer—upright and stalwart—righteousness rivaling ancient heroes.
translations.idiomatic: The edict praised Ding Mu's iron loyalty though captured.

sentences.zh: 其喪柩始反，言尋傷悼。

translations.literal: As his coffin first returns—words soon turn to grief.
translations.idiomatic: His bier has only now come home—our grief is fresh.

sentences.zh: 可贈龍驤將軍、雍州刺史，賻賜一依周虓故事。

translations.literal: Posthumously award General of Dragon Cavaliers—Inspector of Yong Province—burial gifts follow wholly the precedent of Zhou Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Post him Dragon Cavalry general and Yong inspector—gifts like Zhou Xiao's.

sentences.zh: 為立屋宅，並給其妻衣食，以終厥身。」

translations.literal: Build him a dwelling—provide his wife clothing and food for life."
translations.idiomatic: Build his widow a house and support her for life."

sentences.zh: 辛恭靖

translations.literal: Xin Gongjing
translations.idiomatic: Xin Gongjing

sentences.zh: 辛恭靖，隴西狄道人也。

translations.literal: Xin Gongjing was a man of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Gongjing came from Didao in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 少有器幹，才量過人。

translations.literal: In youth he had talent and capacity—his caliber exceeded others.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted and capable beyond peers.

sentences.zh: 隆安中，為河南太守。

translations.literal: During Long'an he was Administrator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Long'an era: Henan prefect.

sentences.zh: 會姚興來寇，恭靖固守百餘日，以無救而陷，被執至長安。

translations.literal: When Yao Xing invaded—Gongjing held firm over a hundred days—with no relief he fell—captured to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing besieged him over one hundred days; without aid the city fell and Xin went to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 興謂之曰：「朕將任卿以東南之事，可乎？

translations.literal: Xing said to him: "I intend to entrust you with southeastern affairs—may it be?"
translations.idiomatic: "Will you run the southeast for me?" asked Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 」恭靖厲色曰：「我寧為國家鬼，不為羌賊臣。

translations.literal: Gongjing replied sternly: "I would rather be a ghost for my state than minister to Qiang bandits."
translations.idiomatic: "I would rather haunt Jin than serve your Qiang throne."

sentences.zh: 」興怒，幽之別室。

translations.literal: Xing was furious—confined him in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing jailed him apart.

sentences.zh: 經三年，至元興中，誑守者，乃逾垣而遁，歸於江東，安帝嘉之。

translations.literal: After three years—in Yuanxing—he deceived the guards—climbed the wall and fled—returned to Jiangdong—Emperor An praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he tricked his guards, scaled the wall, and fled east; Emperor An honored him.

sentences.zh: 桓玄請為諮議參軍，置之朝首。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan requested him as advisory aide—placed him at the head of court.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan made him senior adviser at court.

sentences.zh: 尋而病卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died ill soon after.

sentences.zh: 羅企生

translations.literal: Luo Qisheng
translations.idiomatic: Luo Qisheng

sentences.zh: 羅企生，字宗伯，豫章人也。

translations.literal: Luo Qisheng, courtesy name Zongbo, was a man of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Qisheng, style Zongbo, came from Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 多才藝。

translations.literal: He had many talents and arts.
translations.idiomatic: Versatile and accomplished.

sentences.zh: 初拜佐著作郎，以家貧親老，求補臨汝令，刺史王凝之請為別駕。

translations.literal: First appointed Assistant Editorial Director—because family was poor and parents aged—sought appointment as magistrate of Linru—Inspector Wang Ningzhi requested him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He began as editorial assistant—then took Linru magistrate to support aged parents—Wang Ningzhi wanted him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 殷仲堪之鎮江陵，引為功曹。

translations.literal: When Yin Zhongkan governed Jiangling—appointed him merit evaluator.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongkan made him merit secretary at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 累遷武陵太守。

translations.literal: Promoted by stages to Administrator of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Wuling prefect.

sentences.zh: 未之郡而桓玄攻仲堪，仲堪更以企生為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Before reaching the commandery Huan Xuan attacked Zhongkan—Zhongkan again appointed Qisheng advisory aide.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached his post Xuan struck Zhongkan, who kept him as adviser.

sentences.zh: 仲堪多疑少決，企生深憂之，謂弟遵生曰：「殷侯仁而無斷，事必無成。

translations.literal: Zhongkan was suspicious and hesitant—Qisheng deeply worried—told younger brother Zunsheng: "Lord Yin is benevolent yet cannot decide—affairs will surely fail.
translations.idiomatic: He warned his brother: "Yin is kind but indecisive—this will collapse.

sentences.zh: 成敗，天也，吾當死生以之。

translations.literal: Success and failure belong to Heaven—I shall live or die with him.
translations.idiomatic: Win or lose—Heaven decides—I stay with him to the end."

sentences.zh: 」仲堪果走，文武無送者，唯企生從焉。

translations.literal: Zhongkan indeed fled—civil and military saw none off—only Qisheng followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin fled, officials deserted—only Luo Qisheng rode with him.

sentences.zh: 路經家門，遵生曰：「作如此分離，何可不執手！

translations.literal: Passing his gate—Zunsheng said: "Such a parting—how can we not clasp hands!"
translations.idiomatic: At their gate Zunsheng cried: "We must clasp hands before we part!"

sentences.zh: 」企生回馬授手，遵生有勇力，便牽下之，謂曰：「家有老母，將欲何之？

translations.literal: Qisheng wheeled his horse and offered his hand—Zunsheng had strength—pulled him down—said: "We have an old mother at home—where do you think you go?"
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng turned back; his strong brother dragged him down—"Mother needs us—where are you going?"

sentences.zh: 」企生揮淚曰：「今日之事，我必死之。

translations.literal: Qisheng brushed tears: "Today's affair—I must die.
translations.idiomatic: Through tears: "Today I die—that is settled.

sentences.zh: 汝等奉養不失子道，一門之中有忠與孝，亦復何恨！

translations.literal: You others support her without failing son's duty—in one household having both loyalty and filial piety—what regret remains!
translations.idiomatic: You stay filial at home—I die loyal abroad—both duties shine—why sorrow?"

sentences.zh: 」遵生抱之愈急。

translations.literal: Zunsheng held him tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Zunsheng gripped him harder.

sentences.zh: 仲堪于路待之，企生遙呼曰：「生死是同，願少見待。

translations.literal: Zhongkan waited on the road—Qisheng called from afar: "Life and death are one—please wait a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Yin waited down the road; Qisheng shouted: "We share one fate—give me a breath.

sentences.zh: 」仲堪見企生無脫理，策馬而去。

translations.literal: Zhongkan saw Qisheng could not escape—spurred horse and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no escape for Qisheng, Yin galloped away.

sentences.zh: 玄至荊州，人士無不詣者，企生獨不往，而營理仲堪家。

translations.literal: When Xuan reached Jingzhou—notables all paid calls—only Qisheng did not go—but managed Zhongkan's household.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingzhou everyone visited Xuan except Qisheng, who stayed to settle Yin's family.

sentences.zh: 或謂之曰：「玄猜忍之性，未能取卿誠節，若遂不詣，禍必至矣。

translations.literal: Someone told him: "Xuan's suspicious cruelty cannot long reward your integrity—if you never pay court—disaster will surely come.
translations.idiomatic: Friends warned: "Xuan is cruel—skip his summons and you die.

sentences.zh: 」企生正色曰：「我是殷侯吏，見遇以國士，為弟以力見制，遂不我從，不能共殄醜逆，致此奔敗，亦何面目復就桓求生乎！

translations.literal: Qisheng sternly: "I am Lord Yin's officer—he treated me as a national hero—my younger brother restrained me by force—so I could not follow—unable jointly to destroy the traitor—causing this rout—what face to beg Huan for life!
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Yin honored me as a peer—my brother pinned me down—so we lost—what honor is left if I crawl to Huan Xuan?"

sentences.zh: 」玄聞之大怒，然素待企生厚，先遣人謂曰：「若謝我，當釋汝。

translations.literal: Xuan heard—was furious—yet had always treated Qisheng generously—first sent word: "If you apologize—I will release you.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan raged yet owed him favor—messengers offered: "Bow to me and live.

sentences.zh: 」企生曰：「為殷荊州吏，荊州奔亡，存亡未判，何顏復謝！

translations.literal: Qisheng: "As Inspector Yin's officer—with Yin fled—alive or dead unknown—what face to apologize!
translations.idiomatic: "Yin's fate is unknown—how dare I apologize to you!"

sentences.zh: 」玄即收企生，遣人問欲何言，答曰：「文帝殺嵇康，嵇紹為晉忠臣，從公乞一弟，以養老母。

translations.literal: Xuan seized Qisheng at once—sent men asking last words—answered: "When Wei Emperor Wen killed Xi Kang—Xi Shao became Jin's loyal minister—from you I beg one brother spared—to support my old mother.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan arrested him; his last plea echoed Xi Shao—spare my brother for Mother's sake.

sentences.zh: 」玄許之。

translations.literal: Xuan granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 又引企生於前，謂曰：「吾相遇甚厚，何以見負？

translations.literal: Then Xuan brought Qisheng forward—telling him: "We treated each other generously—why have you betrayed me?
translations.idiomatic: Xuan hauled him up and asked why he had broken faith after such kindness.

sentences.zh: 今者死矣！

translations.literal: Now you shall die!
translations.idiomatic: Now you die!

sentences.zh: 」企生對曰：「使君既興晉陽之甲，軍次尋陽，並奉王命，各還所鎮，升壇盟誓，口血未乾，而生奸計。

translations.literal: Qisheng replied: "Inspector—you once raised hosts on the Jinyang precedent—army halted at Xunyang—together received royal command—each returned to his post—ascended the altar and swore alliance—blood on your lips not yet dry—and you conceived treacherous schemes.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "You marched under imperial banners at Xunyang, swore oaths at the altar—blood barely dry—and now plot treason.

sentences.zh: 自傷力劣，不能翦滅凶逆，恨死晚也。

translations.literal: I grieve my strength feeble—unable to extirpate the vicious rebel—I regret only that death comes late.
translations.idiomatic: I lack strength to destroy you—I only regret dying too late."

sentences.zh: 」玄遂害之，時年三十七，眾咸悼焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xuan killed him—aged thirty-seven—all mourned.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan executed him at thirty-seven; everyone grieved.

sentences.zh: 先是，玄以羔裘遺企生母胡氏，及企生遇害，即日焚裘。

translations.literal: Earlier Xuan had presented a lamb-fur robe to Qisheng's mother Lady Hu—when Qisheng suffered execution—that same day she burned the robe.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had once given Lady Hu a lambskin—she burned it the day her son died.

sentences.zh: 張禕

translations.literal: Zhang Yi
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi

sentences.zh: 張禕，吳郡人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi was a man of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi came from Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 少有操行。

translations.literal: In youth he had conduct and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Even young he lived upright.

sentences.zh: 恭帝為琅邪王，以禕為郎中令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong was Prince of Langye—appointed Yi Palace Captain.
translations.idiomatic: As Prince of Langye, Emperor Gong named him palace captain.

sentences.zh: 及帝踐阼，劉裕以禕帝之故吏，素所親信，封藥酒一罌付禕密令鴆帝。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne—Liu Yu because Yi was the emperor's former clerk—long intimate—sealed a jug of poisoned wine—delivered it to Yi with secret order to poison the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: After Gong took the throne, Liu Yu—trusting Yi as an old aide—handed him sealed wine to poison the retired emperor.

sentences.zh: 禕既受命而歎曰：「鴆君而求生，何面目視息世間哉，不如死也！

translations.literal: Yi having received the charge sighed: "Poisoning the ruler yet seeking life—what face to breathe in this world—better to die!
translations.idiomatic: Yi cried: "Murder my lord and live—what face would I show—better die!

sentences.zh: 」因自飲之而死。

translations.literal: Thereupon drank it himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: He swallowed the draught and died.

sentences.zh: 【史論】

translations.literal: 【Historical Commentary】
translations.idiomatic: Historical Commentary

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：中散以膚受見誅，王儀以抗言獲戾，時皆可謂死非其罪也。

translations.literal: The historians say: Zhongsan died on shallow suspicion—Wang Yi suffered for blunt speech—both might be said to have died without deserving their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Kang fell to rumor; Wang Yi died for candor—both deaths seemed unjust.

sentences.zh: 偉元恥臣晉室，延祖甘赴危亡，所由之理雖同，所趣之途即異，而並見稱當世，垂芳竹帛，豈不以君父居在三之極，忠孝為百行之先者乎！

translations.literal: Wang Pou (Weiyuan) was ashamed to serve as Jin's subject—Xi Shao (Yanzu) willingly faced peril and death—the grounds were alike yet paths diverged—both praised in their age—fragrance on bamboo and silk—is it not because lord and father anchor the highest bonds—loyalty and filial piety lead all virtues!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pou refused shameful office under Jin while Xi Shao marched to his death—different roads, equal fame—because ruler and parent crown the three bonds and loyalty and filial duty come first.

sentences.zh: 且裒獨善其身，故得全其孝，而紹兼濟於物，理宜竭其忠，可謂蘭桂異質而齊芳，《韶》《武》殊音而並美。

translations.literal: Moreover Wang Pou cultivated himself alone—therefore preserved filial piety whole—while Xi Shao aided all under Heaven—by principle owed utmost loyalty—one may say orchid and cassia differ in nature yet share fragrance—musics Shao and Wu differ in tone yet both are beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pou withdrew to perfect filial piety; Xi Shao gave himself for the realm—orchid and laurel, different wood but shared perfume—like Shao music and Wu dance, distinct yet equally fine.

sentences.zh: 或有論紹者以死難獲譏，揚榷言之，未為篤論。

translations.literal: Some who judge Xi Shao mock him for dying in crisis—raising the debate—that is not a settled verdict.
translations.idiomatic: Critics sneer at Xi Shao's battlefield death—that shallow verdict misses the point.

sentences.zh: 夫君，天也，天可仇乎！

translations.literal: The lord is Heaven—is Heaven to be hated!
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign is Heaven—do you rail against Heaven?

sentences.zh: 安既享其榮，危乃違其禍，進退無據，何以立人！

translations.literal: In peace enjoying its glory—in peril fleeing its calamity—advance and retreat without footing—how stand as a human!
translations.idiomatic: Feasting in calm yet fleeing danger—what footing is that for a man?

sentences.zh: 嵇生之隕身全節，用此道也。

translations.literal: Thus Master Ji gave body yet preserved integrity—by this Way.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Kang died to keep his integrity whole—that was his path.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：重義輕生，亡軀殉節。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Esteeming righteousness—lightly esteeming life—casting away the body to die for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The hymn praises those who prized duty over breath and died for principle.

sentences.zh: 勁松方操，嚴霜比烈。

translations.literal: Stalwart pine—upright principle—sharp frost matching fierce cold.
translations.idiomatic: Like pine in frost—unyielding in bitter cold.

sentences.zh: 白刃可陵，貞心難折。

translations.literal: White blades may press—chaste heart cannot break.
translations.idiomatic: Steel may threaten—it cannot snap a faithful heart.

sentences.zh: 道光振古，芳流來哲。

translations.literal: Bright virtue shakes antiquity—fragrance flows to later sages.
translations.idiomatic: Their light shakes the ages; their fame reaches later worthies.
